title.zh: 卷96 司馬叡列傳 賨李雄列傳
title.en: Volume 96: Biography of Sima Rui, Biography of Cong Lixiong
title.raw: 卷96 司馬叡列傳 賨李雄列傳 Volume 96: Biography of Sima Rui, Biography of Cong Lixiong

sentences.zh: 僭晉司馬叡 賨李雄

translations.literal: Usurping Jin Sima Rui; Cong Li Xiong
translations.idiomatic: The Usurping Jin: Sima Rui; Cong Li Xiong

sentences.zh: 司馬叡

translations.literal: Sima Rui
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui

sentences.zh: 僭晉司馬叡，字景文，晉將牛金子也。

translations.literal: The usurping Jin Sima Rui, styled Jingwen, was the son of the Jin general Niu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The usurping Jin ruler Sima Rui, styled Jingwen, was a son of the Jin general Niu Jin.

sentences.zh: 初晉宣帝生大將軍、琅邪武王伷，伷生冗從僕射、琅邪恭王覲。

translations.literal: At first the Jin Founder Emperor begat the Grand General, Prince Wu of Langye Zhou; Zhou begat the Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prince Gong of Langye Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Founder Emperor first begat the Grand General, Prince Wu of Langye, Sima Zhou; Zhou in turn begat the Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary, Prince Gong of Langye, Sima Jin.

sentences.zh: 覲妃譙國夏侯氏，字銅環，與金姦通，遂生叡，因冒姓司馬，仍為覲子。

translations.literal: Jin's consort was Lady Xiahou of Qiao, styled Tonghuan; she had an illicit affair with Jin and bore Rui; he therefore falsely took the surname Sima and was still treated as Jin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's consort was Lady Xiahou of Qiao, styled Tonghuan. She had an affair with Niu Jin and bore Rui, who therefore took the surname Sima falsely and was still accounted Jin's son.

sentences.zh: 由是自言河內溫人。

translations.literal: Because of this he claimed to be a man of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he claimed to be from Wen in Henei.

sentences.zh: 初為王世子，又襲爵，拜散騎常侍，頻遷射聲、越騎校尉，左、右軍將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was heir to the princely house, also inherited the title, was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and was frequently promoted to Commandant of the Archers, Commandant of the Flying Cavalry, and General of the Left and Right Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as heir to the princely house, then inherited the title and was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary. He was repeatedly promoted to Commandant of the Archers, Commandant of the Flying Cavalry, and General of the Left and Right Armies.

sentences.zh: 從晉惠帝幸臨漳，其叔繇為成都王穎所殺，叡懼禍，遂走至洛，迎其母俱歸陳國。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Hui of Jin to Linzhang, his uncle Yao was killed by the Prince of Chengdu Ying; Rui feared disaster, fled to Luo, and met his mother to return together to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied Emperor Hui of Jin to Linzhang, his uncle Yao was killed by the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying. Rui feared for his life, fled to Luoyang, and brought his mother back with him to Chen.

translations.literal: Footnote one.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 東海王越收兵下邳，假叡輔國將軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai Yue gathered troops at Xiapi and provisionally appointed Rui General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Donghai, Wang Yue, gathered troops at Xiapi and appointed Rui Acting General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 越謀迎惠帝於長安，復假叡平東將軍、監徐州諸軍事，使鎮下邳。

translations.literal: Yue plotted to welcome Emperor Hui from Chang'an, again provisionally appointed Rui General Who Pacifies the East and Supervisor of all military affairs in Xuzhou, and sent him to garrison Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue planned to welcome Emperor Hui from Chang'an and again appointed Rui Acting General Who Pacifies the East and Supervisor of Military Affairs in Xuzhou, ordering him to garrison Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 尋加安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事、假節，當鎮壽陽，[2]且留下邳。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made General Who Pacifies the East, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yangzhou, with provisional credentials, and was to garrison Shouyang, [2] yet remained at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further promoted to General Who Pacifies the East, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yangzhou, with provisional credentials. He was to garrison Shouyang, [2] but remained at Xiapi for the time being.

sentences.zh: 及越西迎惠帝，留叡鎮後，平東府事。

translations.literal: When Yue went west to welcome Emperor Hui, he left Rui to garrison the rear and manage the affairs of the Pacify-the-East headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue went west to welcome Emperor Hui, he left Rui behind to garrison the rear and handle the affairs of the Pacify-the-East headquarters.

sentences.zh: [3]當遷鎮江東，屬陳敏作亂，叡以兵少因留下邳。

translations.literal: [3] He was to transfer his garrison to Jiangdong; at that time Chen Min rebelled, and because Rui had few troops he therefore remained at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He was due to transfer his garrison to the lands east of the Yangtze. Chen Min then rose in rebellion, and because Rui had too few troops he remained at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 平文帝初，叡自稱晉王，改元建武，立宗廟、社稷，置百官，立子紹為太子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Pingwen, Rui styled himself King of Jin, changed the era name to Jianwu, established ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, installed the hundred officials, and installed his son Shao as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Pingwen, Rui styled himself King of Jin, changed the era name to Jianwu, established ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain, installed the full bureaucracy, and named his son Shao heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 叡以晉王而祀南郊。

translations.literal: Rui as King of Jin sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: As King of Jin, Rui performed the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其年，叡僭即大位，改為大興元年。

translations.literal: That year Rui usurped the supreme position and changed the era to the first year of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Rui usurped the imperial throne and changed the era name to the first year of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 其朝廷之儀，都邑之制，皆準模王者，擬議中國。

translations.literal: The rites of his court and the institutions of his capital all took royal models as standard and were patterned on the Central Domain.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial of his court and the institutions of his capital all followed royal models and were patterned on those of the Central Domain.

sentences.zh: 遂都於丹陽，因孫權之舊所，即禹貢揚州之地，去洛二千七百里。

translations.literal: He then made his capital at Danyang, on the old seat of Sun Quan, the territory of Yangzhou in the Tribute of Yu, twenty-seven hundred li from Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He then established his capital at Danyang, on the former seat of Sun Quan—the territory of Yangzhou in the Tribute of Yu—twenty-seven hundred li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 地多山水，陽鳥攸居，厥土惟塗泥，厥田惟下下，所謂「島夷卉服」者也。

translations.literal: The land has much mountain and water; the yang-birds dwell there; its soil is mud, its fields lowest grade—the so-called "island barbarians in flowery dress."
translations.idiomatic: The land is rich in mountains and rivers, where the yang-birds dwell. Its soil is mud, its fields of the lowest grade—the region called "island barbarians in flowery dress."

sentences.zh: 周禮，職方氏掌天下之地，辨其邦國都鄙，四夷、八蠻、七閩、九貉、五戎、六狄之人民與其財用、九穀、六畜之數要，周知其利害。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Director of the Regions oversees the lands under Heaven, distinguishes states, capitals, and districts, and the peoples of the four Yi, eight Man, seven Min, nine He, five Rong, and six Di, with their wealth and goods, the tallies of the nine grains and six livestock, and thoroughly knows their benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Rites of Zhou, the Director of the Regions oversees all lands under Heaven, distinguishes states, capitals, and districts, and keeps account of the peoples of the four Yi, eight Man, seven Min, nine He, five Rong, and six Di, together with their wealth, the tallies of the nine grains and six livestock, and knows thoroughly where advantage and harm lie.

sentences.zh: 東南曰揚州，其山鎮曰會稽，其藪澤曰具區，其川三江，其浸五湖，其利金錫竹箭，其民二男五女，其畜宜鳥獸，其穀宜稻。

translations.literal: The southeast is called Yangzhou; its mountain guardian is Kuaiji; its marshes and lakes are Juchu; its rivers are the Three Rivers; its marshes are the Five Lakes; its products are gold, tin, bamboo, and arrows; its people are two men to five women; its livestock suit birds and beasts; its grain suits rice.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast is called Yangzhou. Its guardian mountain is Kuaiji; its marshes and lakes are Juchu; its rivers are the Three Rivers; its great marshes are the Five Lakes. Its products are gold, tin, bamboo, and arrows; its people number two men to five women; its livestock suit birds and beasts; its grain suits rice.

sentences.zh: 春秋時為吳越之地。

translations.literal: In Spring and Autumn times it was the land of Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn period it was the territory of Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 吳越僭號稱王，僻遠一隅，不聞華土。

translations.literal: Wu and Yue usurped titles and styled themselves kings, remote in a corner, unheard of in the Central Domain.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Yue usurped royal titles in a remote corner of the realm, unknown to the Central Domain.

sentences.zh: 楚申公巫臣竊妻以奔，教其軍陣，然後乃知戰伐。

translations.literal: Chu Grandee Wuchen of Shen stole a wife and fled there, taught them army formations, and only then did they learn warfare.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchen, Grandee of Shen in Chu, fled there after stealing another man's wife, he taught them military formations—and only then did they learn the arts of war.

sentences.zh: 由是晚與中國交通。

translations.literal: From this they were late in having contact with the Central Domain.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason they came into contact with the Central Domain only late.

sentences.zh: 俗氣輕急，不識禮教，盛飾子女以招遊客，此其土風也。

translations.literal: Their customs are light and hasty; they do not know ritual teaching; they lavishly adorn sons and daughters to attract travelers—such is their local character.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs are restless and impulsive; they know little of ritual instruction; they lavish adornment on sons and daughters to attract visitors—such is the local character.

sentences.zh: 戰國時則并於楚。

translations.literal: In Warring States times it was annexed by Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Warring States period it was absorbed by Chu.

sentences.zh: 故地遠恃險，世亂則先叛，世治則後服。

translations.literal: Therefore the land is remote and relies on terrain; in ages of disorder it rebels first, in ages of order it submits last.
translations.idiomatic: The region is remote and relies on natural barriers: in troubled times it rebels first, in peaceful times it submits last.

sentences.zh: 秦末，項羽起江南，故衡山王吳芮從百越之兵，越王無諸身率閩中之眾以從，滅秦。

translations.literal: At the end of Qin, Xiang Yu rose in Jiangnan; the former King of Hengshan Wu Rui followed with the armies of the Hundred Yue; the King of Yue Wuzhu personally led the masses of Minzhong to follow and destroyed Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qin dynasty, Xiang Yu rose in Jiangnan. The former King of Hengshan, Wu Rui, followed with the armies of the Hundred Yue, and the King of Yue, Wuzhu, personally led the people of Minzhong in the campaign that overthrew Qin.

sentences.zh: 漢初，封芮為長沙王，無諸為閩越王，又封吳王濞於朱方。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Rui was enfeoffed as King of Changsha, Wuzhu as King of Minyue, and the King of Wu Pi was also enfeoffed at Zhufang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty, Rui was enfeoffed as King of Changsha, Wuzhu as King of Minyue, and Liu Pi as King of Wu at Zhufang.

sentences.zh: 逆亂相尋，亟見夷滅。

translations.literal: Rebellions followed one after another, and they were soon extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions followed one upon another, and they were soon destroyed.

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，孫權遂與劉備分據吳蜀。

translations.literal: At the great disorder at the end of Han, Sun Quan then with Liu Bei divided and held Wu and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the great disorder at the end of the Han, Sun Quan and Liu Bei divided and held Wu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 權阻長江，殆天地所以限內外也。

translations.literal: Quan blocked by the Yangtze—almost what Heaven and Earth use to divide inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Quan held the line of the Yangtze—almost the boundary Heaven and Earth set between inner and outer realms.

sentences.zh: 叡因擾亂，跨而有之。

translations.literal: Rui, taking advantage of the turmoil, straddled and possessed it.
translations.idiomatic: Rui seized the region amid the turmoil and held it.

sentences.zh: 中原冠帶呼江東之人，皆為貉子，若狐貉類云。

translations.literal: The gentry of the Central Plain called the people east of the Yangtze all 'Hezi,' like fox and raccoon-dog sorts.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry of the Central Plain called everyone east of the Yangtze 'Hezi'—as though they were foxes and raccoon dogs.

sentences.zh: 巴、蜀、蠻、獠、谿、俚、楚、越，鳥聲禽呼，言語不同，猴蛇魚鼈，嗜慾皆異。

translations.literal: Ba, Shu, Man, Liao, Xi, Li, Chu, and Yue—bird cries and fowl calls, languages not the same; monkeys, snakes, fish, and turtles—all desires different.
translations.idiomatic: Ba, Shu, Man, Liao, Xi, Li, Chu, and Yue peoples cried like birds and beasts; their languages differed, and monkeys, snakes, fish, and turtles—each people's appetites were unlike the next.

sentences.zh: 江山遼闊將數千里，叡羈縻而已，未能制服其民。

translations.literal: Rivers and mountains stretch vast for nearly a thousand li; Rui only kept them on loose reins and could not subdue their people.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and mountains stretched across nearly a thousand li. Rui could only keep them on loose reins and could not truly subdue the people.

sentences.zh: 有水田，少陸種，以罟網為業。

translations.literal: There are paddy fields, little dry-land planting; they take net-fishing as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: There were paddy fields but little dry-land farming; net-fishing was their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 機巧趨利，恩義寡薄。

translations.literal: Clever and quick to pursue profit; kindness and righteousness thin.
translations.idiomatic: They were clever and quick to pursue profit, but thin in kindness and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 家無藏蓄，常守饑寒。

translations.literal: Households have no stored reserves; they constantly keep to hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Households kept no stores and lived perpetually on the edge of hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 地既暑濕，多有腫泄之病，障氣毒霧，射工、沙蝨、蛇虺之害，無所不有。

translations.literal: The land being hot and damp, there are many swelling and diarrhea illnesses; barrier miasma, poisonous fog, and the harms of the shooting insect, sand mite, snakes and vipers—there is nothing not present.
translations.idiomatic: The land was hot and damp, and swelling and diarrhea were common. Barrier miasmas, poisonous fogs, and the harms of shooting insects, sand mites, snakes, and vipers were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 叡割有揚、荊、梁三州之土，因其故地，分置十數州及諸郡縣，郡縣戶口至有不滿百者。

translations.literal: Rui carved out the territory of Yang, Jing, and Liang provinces, and according to the old lands divided and set up more than ten provinces and various commanderies and counties; some commanderies and counties had registered households not even reaching a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Rui carved out the lands of Yang, Jing, and Liang provinces, and following the old boundaries divided them into more than ten provinces with their commanderies and counties—some districts had fewer than a hundred registered households.

sentences.zh: 遣使韓暢浮海來請通和。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy Han Chang by sea to request communication and peace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the envoy Han Chang across the sea to request peaceful relations.

sentences.zh: 平文皇帝以其僭立江表，拒不納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Pingwen, because he had usurped establishment south of the Yangtze, refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen refused the overture, on the grounds that Rui had usurped power south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 是時叡大將軍王敦宗族擅勢，權重於叡，迭為上下，了無君臣之分。

translations.literal: At this time Rui's Grand General Wang Dun's clan monopolized power; their authority weighed heavier than Rui's; they alternated as superior and inferior, entirely without distinction of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Rui's Grand General Wang Dun and his clan monopolized power. Their authority outweighed the emperor's; they alternated as master and servant, with no trace of proper lord-and-minister relations.

sentences.zh: 叡侍中劉隗言於叡曰：「王氏強大，宜漸抑損。」

translations.literal: Rui's Palace Attendant Liu Wei said to Rui: 'The Wang clan is powerful; they should gradually be restrained and reduced.'
translations.idiomatic: Rui's Palace Attendant Liu Wei said to him, 'The Wang clan is too powerful. They should be restrained step by step.'

sentences.zh: 敦聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Dun heard and hated it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun heard of this, he was enraged.

sentences.zh: 惠帝時，叡改年曰永昌。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Hui, Rui changed the era name to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Hui, Rui changed the era name to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 王敦先鎮武昌，乃表於叡曰：「劉隗前在門下，遂秉權寵。

translations.literal: Wang Dun first garrisoned Wuchang, then memorialized Rui: 'Liu Wei formerly at the gate, then grasped power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, who had first garrisoned Wuchang, then memorialized Rui: 'Liu Wei, once a mere gate attendant, has seized power and imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 今趣進軍，[4]指討姦孽，宜速斬隗首，以謝遠近。

translations.literal: Now I urge the army forward, [4] aiming to punish treacherous villains; you should quickly behead Wei and present his head to appease near and far.
translations.idiomatic: I now press the army forward [4] to punish treacherous villains. You should swiftly behead Wei and present his head to satisfy both near and far.

sentences.zh: 朝梟隗首，諸軍夕退。

translations.literal: If the court displays Wei's head in the morning, the armies will withdraw by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Display Wei's head at court in the morning, and the armies will withdraw by evening.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲不能遵明湯典，顛覆厥度，幸納伊尹之訓，殷道復昌，賢智故有先失後得者矣。」

translations.literal: Formerly Taijia could not follow and clarify the ordinances of Tang, overturned his standards; fortunately he accepted the instruction of Yi Yin, and the Way of Yin flourished again—thus the wise know there are those who first lose and later gain.'
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Taijia could not uphold the ordinances of Tang and overturned the established order; only by accepting Yi Yin's instruction did the Yin dynasty flourish again. The wise know that one may err first and recover later.'

sentences.zh: 敦又移告州郡，以沈充為大都督，護東吳諸軍。

translations.literal: Dun also sent notices to the provinces and commanderies, making Shen Chong Grand Commander-in-Chief and Protector of all armies in Eastern Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Dun also sent notices to the provinces and commanderies, appointing Shen Chong Grand Commander-in-Chief and Protector of all armies in Eastern Wu.

sentences.zh: 叡乃下書曰：「王敦恃寵，敢肆狂逆，方朕於太甲，欲見囚于桐宮。

translations.literal: Rui then issued a writ: 'Wang Dun, relying on favor, dares to unleash madness and rebellion, compares me to Taijia, and wishes to see me imprisoned in the Tong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Rui then issued an edict: 'Wang Dun, relying on imperial favor, dares to run riot in rebellion. He compares me to Taijia and wishes to imprison me in the Tong Palace.

sentences.zh: 是可忍也，孰不可忍也！

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be borne!
translations.idiomatic: If this can be borne, what cannot be borne!

sentences.zh: 今當親帥六軍，以誅大逆。」

translations.literal: Now I shall personally lead the Six Armies to execute the great rebel.'
translations.idiomatic: I shall now personally lead the Six Armies to execute this arch-rebel.'

sentences.zh: 叡光祿勳王含率其子瑜以輕舟棄叡，歸于武昌。

translations.literal: Rui's Household Minister of the Left Wang Han led his son Yu in light boats, abandoned Rui, and returned to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's Household Minister of the Left Wang Han took his son Yu aboard light boats, abandoned the emperor, and fled to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 叡以其司空王導為前鋒大都督，尚書陸曄為軍司；

translations.literal: Rui made his Minister of Works Wang Dao Vanguard Grand Commander-in-Chief, and the Master of Writing Lu Ye army supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: Rui appointed his Minister of Works Wang Dao Vanguard Grand Commander-in-Chief and the Master of Writing Lu Ye army supervisor;

sentences.zh: 以廣州刺史陶侃為江州，梁州刺史甘卓為荊州，使其率眾掎躡敦後；

translations.literal: he made the Inspector of Guangzhou Tao Kan commander of Jiangzhou, the Inspector of Liangzhou Gan Zhuo commander of Jingzhou, and ordered them to lead their masses to strike at Dun's rear;
translations.idiomatic: he made the Inspector of Guangzhou Tao Kan commander of Jiang Province and the Inspector of Liangzhou Gan Zhuo commander of Jing Province, ordering them to lead their forces against Dun's rear;

sentences.zh: 以太子右率周莚率中軍三千人討沈充。

translations.literal: he made the Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Household Zhou Yan lead three thousand men of the Central Army to attack Shen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: and he ordered the Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Household Zhou Yan to lead three thousand Central Army troops against Shen Chong.

sentences.zh: 敦至洌州，表尚書令刁協黨附，宜加誅戮。

translations.literal: Dun reached Lizhou and memorialized that the Master of Writing Diao Xie was partisan and should be further punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun reached Lizhou, he memorialized that the Master of Writing Diao Xie was a partisan and should be executed.

sentences.zh: 叡遣右將軍周札戍于石頭，札潛與敦書，許軍至為應。

translations.literal: Rui sent the General of the Right Zhou Zha to garrison Shitou; Zha secretly wrote to Dun, promising to respond when the army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent the General of the Right Zhou Zha to garrison Shitou. Zha secretly wrote to Dun, promising to act in concert when the army arrived.

sentences.zh: 敦使司馬楊朗等入于石頭。

translations.literal: Dun sent his Major Yang Lang and others into Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Dun sent his Major Yang Lang and others into Shitou.

sentences.zh: 札□見敦。

translations.literal: Zha saw Dun; the text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Zha saw Dun; the text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 朗等既據石頭，叡征西將軍戴淵、鎮北將軍劉隗率眾攻之，戴淵親率士，鼓眾陵城。

translations.literal: Lang and others having seized Shitou, Rui's General Who Pacifies the West Dai Yuan and General Who Pacifies the North Liu Wei led masses to attack; Dai Yuan personally led soldiers, drummed the masses to scale the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lang and the others held Shitou, Rui's General Who Pacifies the West Dai Yuan and General Who Pacifies the North Liu Wei led troops to attack. Dai Yuan personally led his men and drummed the army forward to storm the walls.

sentences.zh: 俄而鼓止息，朗等乘之，叡軍敗績。

translations.literal: Soon the drums ceased; Lang and others seized the moment, and Rui's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the drums fell silent. Lang and his men seized the moment, and Rui's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 隗、協入見叡，叡遣其避禍，二人泣而出。

translations.literal: Wei and Xie entered to see Rui; Rui sent them to avoid disaster; the two wept as they went out.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Xie came before Rui, who urged them to flee for their lives. The two left in tears.

sentences.zh: 隗還淮陰，後奔石勒。

translations.literal: Wei returned to Huaiyin and later fled to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Wei returned to Huaiyin and later fled to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 協奔江乘，為敦追兵所害。

translations.literal: Xie fled to Jiangcheng and was harmed by Dun's pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xie fled toward Jiangcheng and was killed by Dun's pursuing troops.

sentences.zh: 叡師敗。

translations.literal: Rui's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 敦自為丞相，武昌郡公，邑萬戶，朝事大小皆關諮之。

translations.literal: Dun made himself Chancellor, Duke of Wuchang Commandery, fief of ten thousand households; great and small court matters all had to be referred to him for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Dun made himself Chancellor and Duke of Wuchang Commandery with a fief of ten thousand households. Great and small matters of state all required his approval.

sentences.zh: 敦收戴淵及叡尚書左僕射周顗，並斬于石頭，皆叡朝之望也。

translations.literal: Dun seized Dai Yuan and Rui's Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhou Yi and beheaded them both at Shitou—all pillars of Rui's court.
translations.idiomatic: Dun seized Dai Yuan and Rui's Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhou Yi and beheaded them at Shitou—men who had been pillars of the court.

sentences.zh: 於是改易百官及諸州鎮，其餘轉徙黜免者過百數，或朝行暮改，或百日半年。

translations.literal: Thereupon he changed the hundred officials and the various provincial garrisons; the rest transferred, moved, dismissed, or removed exceeded a hundred—some changed morning to evening, some in a hundred days or half a year.
translations.idiomatic: He then reshuffled the bureaucracy and provincial garrisons. More than a hundred officials were transferred, demoted, or dismissed—some overnight, others over the course of months.

sentences.zh: 敦所寵沈充、錢鳳等所言必用，所譖必死。

translations.literal: Those Dun favored—Shen Chong, Qian Feng, and the like—whatever they said was adopted; whomever they slandered was sure to die.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Shen Chong, Qian Feng, and Dun's other favorites recommended was adopted; whoever they slandered was doomed.

sentences.zh: 敦將還武昌，其長史謝鯤曰：「公不朝，懼天下私議。」

translations.literal: Dun was about to return to Wuchang; his Chief Clerk Xie Kun said: 'If my lord does not attend court, I fear private discussion throughout the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: When Dun was about to return to Wuchang, his Chief Clerk Xie Kun said, 'If you do not attend court, my lord, the realm will surely whisper against you.'

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「君能保無變乎？」

translations.literal: Dun said: 'Can you guarantee there will be no change?'
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, 'Can you guarantee nothing will go wrong?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「鯤近入覲，主上側席待公，遲得相見，宮省穆然，必無不虞之慮。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Kun recently entered audience; the sovereign waited on the edge of his seat for my lord; though meeting was delayed, the palace offices were tranquil—surely there is no worry of the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Kun replied, 'When I recently attended court, His Majesty waited impatiently for you. Though the meeting was delayed, the palace was calm. There is surely no cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 公若入朝，鯤請侍從。」

translations.literal: If my lord enters court, Kun requests to attend and follow.'
translations.idiomatic: If you enter court, my lord, I beg to attend you.'

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「正復殺君等數百，何損朝廷！」

translations.literal: Dun said: 'Even if I kill several hundred of you gentlemen, what harm to the court!'
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, 'Even if I kill several hundred of you, what harm would that do the court!'

sentences.zh: 遂不朝而去。

translations.literal: He then did not attend court and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He then left without attending court.

sentences.zh: 敦召安南將軍甘卓，轉譙王承為軍司，並不從。

translations.literal: Dun summoned the General Who Pacifies the South Gan Zhuo and transferred the Prince of Qiao Cheng to army supervisor; neither obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Dun summoned the General Who Pacifies the South Gan Zhuo and tried to transfer the Prince of Qiao Cheng to army supervisor; neither obeyed.

sentences.zh: 敦遣從母弟南蠻校尉魏乂率江夏太守李恒攻承於臨湘，旬日城陷，執承送于武昌。

translations.literal: Dun sent his cousin on his mother's side, Commandant of the Southern Man Wei Yi, leading the Administrator of Jiangxia Li Heng to attack Cheng at Linxiang; in ten days the city fell; they seized Cheng and sent him to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Dun sent his maternal cousin, Commandant of the Southern Man Wei Yi, with the Administrator of Jiangxia Li Heng to attack Cheng at Linxiang. Within ten days the city fell; they seized Cheng and sent him to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 敦從弟王廙使賊迎之，害于車中。

translations.literal: Dun's cousin Wang Yi sent bandits to meet him and killed him in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's cousin Wang Yi sent assassins to intercept him and killed him in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 先是，王敦表疏，言旨不遜，叡以示承曰：「敦言如此，豈有厭哉？」

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Dun's memorials were disrespectful in tone; Rui showed them to Cheng and said: 'Dun speaks thus—can he have had enough?'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Dun's memorials had been disrespectful in tone. Rui showed them to Cheng and said, 'Dun speaks like this—can he ever have enough?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下不早裁之，難將作矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'If Your Majesty does not cut him down early, disaster will arise.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, 'If Your Majesty does not restrain him soon, disaster will follow.'

sentences.zh: 敦惡之。

translations.literal: Dun hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Dun hated him for this.

sentences.zh: 襄陽太守周慮襲殺甘卓。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Xiangyang Zhou Lü ambushed and killed Gan Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Xiangyang Zhou Lü ambushed and killed Gan Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 叡畏迫於敦，居常憂戚，發病而死。

translations.literal: Rui, cowed by Dun, lived in constant worry and grief, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, cowed by Dun, lived in constant anxiety and grief until illness carried him off.

sentences.zh: 子紹僭立，改年曰太寧。

translations.literal: His son Shao usurped the throne and changed the era to Taining.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao usurped the throne and changed the era name to Taining.

sentences.zh: 王敦將篡，諷紹徵己，乃為書曰：「孤子紹頓首。

translations.literal: Wang Dun was about to usurp; he hinted to Shao to summon him, and composed a letter: 'The orphan Shao bows his head.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was plotting usurpation and prompted Shao to summon him. He drafted a letter: 'The orphan Shao bows his head.

sentences.zh: 天下事大，紹以眇身，弗克負荷，哀憂孔疚，如臨于谷，實賴冢宰，以濟艱難。

translations.literal: The affairs of the realm are great; Shao with his slight person cannot bear the burden; sorrow and worry are piercing, as if facing a ravine; I truly rely on the chief minister to cross the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of the realm are weighty, and I, Shao, am too slight to bear them. My grief is piercing, as though I stood at the edge of a ravine. I truly rely on the chief minister to carry us through these hardships.

sentences.zh: 公邁德樹勳，遐邇歸懷，任社稷之託，居總己之統，然道里長遠，江川阻深，動有介石之機，而回旋之間，固以有所喪矣。

translations.literal: My lord's far-reaching virtue and established merit make near and far turn in allegiance; you bear the trust of the altars and occupy the overall governance, yet the roads are long and rivers deep; movement has the moment of the jie stone, yet in turning there is certainly some loss.
translations.idiomatic: Your far-reaching virtue and established merit draw allegiance from near and far. You bear the trust of the altars and hold overall governance. Yet the roads are long and the rivers deep; every move has its decisive moment, and in turning back and forth something is always lost.

sentences.zh: 謂公宜入輔朝政，得旦夕詶諮，朝士亦僉以為然。

translations.literal: I say my lord should enter to assist court governance, obtaining morning and evening consultation; the court gentlemen also all deem it so.
translations.idiomatic: I believe you should enter court to assist in governance, so that we may consult morning and evening. The court gentlemen are unanimous in this view.

sentences.zh: 以公高亮忠肅，至心憂國，苟其宜然，便當以至公處之，期於靜國寧民，要之括囊無咎。

translations.literal: Because my lord is lofty, bright, loyal, and reverent, with utmost heart worrying for the state—if it is fitting, then with utmost fairness treat it, expecting to quiet the state and pacify the people; in sum, keep the bag closed without blame.
translations.idiomatic: Because you are lofty, loyal, and reverent, with the utmost concern for the state—if this is fitting, it should be handled with perfect fairness, in the hope of quieting the realm and pacifying the people. In the end, keep your counsel folded and you will be without blame.

sentences.zh: 伏想闇同此志，願便速剋近期，以副翹企之懷。」

translations.literal: I humbly think you secretly share this will; I wish you quickly to fix a near date to answer the eager expectation.'
translations.idiomatic: I trust you share this intent in secret. I beg you to set a near date at once, to satisfy our eager hopes.'

sentences.zh: 紹恭憚於敦若此。

translations.literal: Shao was so deferential and in awe of Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Shao's deference and fear of Dun.

sentences.zh: 復使兼太常應詹拜敦丞相、武昌郡公，奏事不名，入朝不趨，劍履上殿。

translations.literal: He again sent the Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Ying Zhan to invest Dun as Chancellor, Duke of Wuchang Commandery, memorials without using his name, court entry without hastening, sword and shoes on the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent the Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Ying Zhan to invest Dun as Chancellor and Duke of Wuchang Commandery, with the privileges of memorializing without using his name, entering court without hastening, and wearing sword and shoes in the hall.

sentences.zh: 敦於是屯於蕪湖。

translations.literal: Dun then encamped at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then encamped at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 敦乃轉王導為司徒，自領揚州刺史，以兄含子應為武衞將軍，以自副貳。

translations.literal: Dun then transferred Wang Dao to Minister of Education, himself took the post of Inspector of Yangzhou, and made his brother Han's son Ying General of the Martial Guard as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then transferred Wang Dao to Minister of Education, took the post of Inspector of Yangzhou himself, and appointed his brother Han's son Ying General of the Martial Guard as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 敦無子，養應為後。

translations.literal: Dun had no son and adopted Ying as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had no sons and adopted Ying as his heir.

sentences.zh: 敦疾踰年，故召含還，欲屬以後事。

translations.literal: Dun's illness exceeded a year; therefore he summoned Han back, wishing to entrust him with later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had been ill for more than a year, so he summoned Han back, intending to entrust him with affairs after his death.

sentences.zh: 是時敦令紹宿衞之兵三番休二。

translations.literal: At this time Dun ordered Shao's palace-guard troops three rotations rest two.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Dun ordered that Shao's palace-guard troops rotate three shifts with two off.

sentences.zh: 紹密欲襲敦，微行察敦營壘。

translations.literal: Shao secretly wished to strike Dun and went in disguise to inspect Dun's camps and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Shao secretly planned to strike Dun and went in disguise to inspect his camps.

sentences.zh: 及敦疾，紹屢遣大臣訊問起居，遷含驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Dun fell ill, Shao repeatedly sent great ministers to inquire after his health and promoted Han to General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun fell ill, Shao repeatedly sent high ministers to inquire after his health and promoted Han to General of Agile Cavalry with the privileges of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 敦疾甚，紹召其司徒王導、中書監庾亮、丹陽尹溫嶠、尚書卞壼密謀討之。

translations.literal: Dun's illness was severe; Shao summoned his Minister of Education Wang Dao, Palace Secretariat Supervisor Yu Liang, Intendant of Danyang Wen Jiao, and Master of Writing Bian Huai to plot secretly to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun's illness grew severe, Shao secretly summoned his Minister of Education Wang Dao, Palace Secretariat Supervisor Yu Liang, Intendant of Danyang Wen Jiao, and Master of Writing Bian Huai to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 導、嶠及右將軍卞敦共據石頭，光祿勳應詹都督朱雀桁南諸軍事，尚書令郗鑒都督從駕諸軍事，紹出次于中堂。

translations.literal: Dao, Jiao, and General of the Right Bian Dun together held Shitou; Household Minister Ying Zhan commanded all military affairs south of the Vermilion Bird Bridge; Master of Writing Xi Jian commanded all military affairs accompanying the imperial carriage; Shao went out and encamped at the Central Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Dao, Jiao, and General of the Right Bian Dun held Shitou together. Household Minister Ying Zhan commanded all troops south of the Vermilion Bird Bridge, Master of Writing Xi Jian commanded the imperial escort, and Shao encamped at the Central Hall.

sentences.zh: 敦聞兵起，怒，欲自將，困不能坐。

translations.literal: Dun heard troops had risen, was angry, wished to lead in person, but was so weakened he could not sit.
translations.idiomatic: When Dun heard that troops had risen against him, he was furious and wished to lead in person, but was too weak even to sit up.

sentences.zh: 召其黨錢鳳、鄧岳、周撫等率眾三萬指造建業。

translations.literal: He summoned his partisans Qian Feng, Deng Yue, Zhou Fu, and others to lead masses of thirty thousand straight toward Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned his partisans Qian Feng, Deng Yue, Zhou Fu, and others to lead thirty thousand men straight toward Jianye.

sentences.zh: 含謂敦曰：「此事吾便當行。」

translations.literal: Han said to Dun: 'In this matter I myself shall go.'
translations.idiomatic: Han said to Dun, "I shall handle this matter myself."

sentences.zh: 於是以含為元帥。

translations.literal: Thereupon Han was made supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Han was then made supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 鳳等問敦曰：「事克之日，天子云何？」

translations.literal: Feng and others asked Dun: 'On the day the affair succeeds, what of the Son of Heaven?'
translations.idiomatic: Feng and the others asked Dun, "When the affair succeeds, what shall be done with the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 敦曰：「尚未南郊，何為天子！

translations.literal: Dun said: 'He has not yet sacrificed at the southern suburb—what makes him Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Dun said, "He has not yet performed the southern suburban sacrifice—what makes him Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 便盡卿兵勢，唯保護東海王及裴妃而已。」

translations.literal: Then exhaust your military power, only protecting the Prince of Donghai and Consort Pei, that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: Deploy all your military strength, but protect only the Prince of Donghai and Consort Pei."

sentences.zh: 初，紹謂敦已死，故敢發兵。

translations.literal: Earlier Shao thought Dun was already dead, and therefore dared to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shao had believed Dun was already dead, and therefore dared to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 及下詔數日，敦猶能與王導書，後自手筆曰：「太真別來幾日，作如此事！」

translations.literal: Several days after the edict was issued, Dun could still write to Wang Dao; later in his own hand he wrote: 'Taizhen, how many days since we parted, and you do such a thing!'
translations.idiomatic: Several days after the edict was issued, Dun could still write to Wang Dao. Later he added in his own hand, "Taizhen, how many days since we parted, and you do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 太真，溫嶠字也。

translations.literal: Taizhen was Wen Jiao's style.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhen was Wen Jiao's style name.

sentences.zh: 紹朝見之，咸共駭懼。

translations.literal: Shao saw it at court audience; all together were shocked and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao saw it at court, everyone was shocked and afraid.

sentences.zh: 含等兵至，溫嶠輒燒朱雀桁以挫其鋒。

translations.literal: When Han's troops arrived, Wen Jiao immediately burned the Vermilion Bird Bridge to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: When Han's troops arrived, Wen Jiao immediately burned the Vermilion Bird Bridge to blunt their advance.

sentences.zh: 紹使中軍司馬曹渾、左衞參軍陳嵩、段匹磾弟禿率壯士千人逆含等，戰于江寧，斬其前鋒將何康，殺數百人。

translations.literal: Shao sent Central Army Major Cao Hun, Left Guard Adjutant Chen Song, and Duan Pidi's brother Tu to lead a thousand stalwart men against Han and others; they fought at Jiangning, beheaded their vanguard general He Kang, and killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Central Army Major Cao Hun, Left Guard Adjutant Chen Song, and Duan Pidi's brother Tu with a thousand stalwart men against Han's forces. They fought at Jiangning, beheaded the vanguard general He Kang, and killed several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 敦聞康死，軍不獲濟，怒曰：「我兄老婢耳！

translations.literal: Dun heard Kang was dead and the army could not cross; angrily he said: 'My elder brother is an old serving-woman!
translations.idiomatic: When Dun heard that Kang was dead and the army could not cross, he raged, "My elder brother is a feeble old woman!

sentences.zh: 門戶衰微，群從中才兼文武者皆早死，今年事去矣。」

translations.literal: The house declines; among the clan those with both civil and military talent all died early—this year's affair is lost.'
translations.idiomatic: Our house is in decline. Every kinsman with both civil and military talent is already dead. This year's affair is lost."

sentences.zh: 語參軍呂寶曰：「我當力行。」

translations.literal: He said to Adjutant Lü Bao: 'I shall exert myself and go.'
translations.idiomatic: He said to Adjutant Lü Bao, "I shall force myself to go."

sentences.zh: 因作勢而起，困乏，乃復臥。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made a show of effort and rose, but was exhausted and weak, and lay down again.
translations.idiomatic: He made as if to rise, but exhaustion overcame him and he lay down again.

sentences.zh: 使術士郭璞筮之，卦成，對曰：「不能佳。」

translations.literal: He had the diviner Guo Pu cast the hexagrams; when the hexagram was complete, he replied: 'It cannot be good.'
translations.idiomatic: He had the diviner Guo Pu cast the hexagrams. When the reading was complete, Guo replied, "It cannot be favorable."

sentences.zh: 敦既疑璞勸亮、嶠等舉事，又聞卦惡，於是殺璞。

translations.literal: Dun already suspected Pu had urged Liang, Jiao, and others to raise the affair, and also heard the hexagram was evil; thereupon he killed Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Dun already suspected that Pu had urged Liang, Jiao, and the others to act. When he heard the ominous reading, he had Pu killed.

sentences.zh: 敦疾轉困，語其舅羊鑒及子應曰：「我亡後，應便即位，先立朝廷百官，然後營葬。」

translations.literal: Dun's illness turned critical; he told his uncle Yang Jian and his son Ying: 'After I die, Ying shall at once take the throne; first install the court's hundred officials, then arrange the burial.'
translations.idiomatic: As Dun's illness grew critical, he told his uncle Yang Jian and his son Ying, "After I die, Ying shall take power at once. First install the court officials, then arrange my burial."

sentences.zh: 初敦敗叡之後，夢白犬自天而下，噬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Dun defeated Rui, he dreamed a white dog came down from Heaven and bit him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Dun had defeated Rui, he dreamed that a white dog descended from Heaven and bit him.

sentences.zh: 及疾甚，見刁協、甘卓為祟，遂死。

translations.literal: When his illness was severe, he saw Diao Xie and Gan Zhuo as apparitions haunting him, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew severe, he saw Diao Xie and Gan Zhuo as vengeful spirits and died.

sentences.zh: 王應祕不發喪，裹屍以席，埋於齋中，與其將諸葛瑤等縱酒淫逸。

translations.literal: Wang Ying secretly did not announce the mourning, wrapped the corpse in matting, buried it in the study, and with his generals Zhuge Yao and others indulged in wine and dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying kept the death secret, wrapped the corpse in matting, buried it in the study, and with his generals Zhuge Yao and others gave themselves to wine and dissipation.

sentences.zh: 沈充將萬餘人來會含等。

translations.literal: Shen Chong led more than ten thousand men to join Han and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong brought more than ten thousand men to join Han's forces.

sentences.zh: 充臨行，顧謂其妻曰：「男兒不建豹尾，不能歸也。」

translations.literal: As Chong was about to depart, he turned and said to his wife: 'A man who does not establish the leopard-tail banner cannot return.'
translations.idiomatic: As Chong was about to depart, he turned to his wife and said, "A man who does not win the leopard-tail banner of command cannot return."

sentences.zh: 紹平西將軍祖約率眾至于淮南，[5]逐敦所置淮南太守任台。

translations.literal: Shao's General Who Pacifies the West Zu Yue led masses to Huainan, [5] expelled Dun's appointed Administrator of Huainan Ren Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's General Who Pacifies the West Zu Yue led his troops to Huainan [5] and expelled Dun's appointed Administrator of Huainan, Ren Tai.

sentences.zh: 紹將劉遐、蘇峻濟自滿洲，含相率渡兵，應詹逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Shao's generals Liu Xia and Su Jun crossed from Manzhou; Han led troops across in succession; Ying Zhan struck them in counterattack and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's generals Liu Xia and Su Jun crossed from Manzhou. Han led his troops across in turn, but Ying Zhan counterattacked and routed them.

sentences.zh: 周撫斬錢鳳，沈充將吳儒斬充。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu beheaded Qian Feng; Shen Chong's general Wu Ru beheaded Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu beheaded Qian Feng, and Shen Chong's general Wu Ru beheaded Chong.

sentences.zh: 紹遣御史劉彝發敦瘞，斬屍，梟首朱雀桁。

translations.literal: Shao sent the Censor Liu Yi to exhume Dun's burial, behead the corpse, and display the head at the Vermilion Bird Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Censor Liu Yi to exhume Dun's body, behead the corpse, and display the head at the Vermilion Bird Bridge.

sentences.zh: 紹死，子衍僭立，號年曰咸和。

translations.literal: Shao died; his son Yan usurped the throne and styled the era Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao died, his son Yan usurped the throne and styled the era Xianhe.

sentences.zh: 衍歷陽太守蘇峻不順於衍，衍護軍庾亮曰：「蘇峻豺狼，終為禍亂，晁錯所謂削之亦反，不削亦反，削之反速而禍小，不削反遲而禍大。」

translations.literal: Yan's Administrator of Liyang Su Jun was not compliant with Yan; Yan's Protector of the Army Yu Liang said: 'Su Jun is a wolf; in the end he will be calamity and disorder—the so-called "if you cut him down he still rebels, if you do not cut him down he still rebels; cut him down and rebellion is swift but the calamity small, do not cut him down and rebellion is slow but the calamity great" of Chao Cuo.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Administrator of Liyang, Su Jun, defied him. Yan's Protector of the Army Yu Liang said, "Su Jun is a wolf who will surely bring disaster. As Chao Cuo said: cut him down and he rebels anyway; leave him and he rebels anyway—but cutting him down brings swift rebellion and small harm, while leaving him brings slow rebellion and great harm."

sentences.zh: 乃以大司農徵之，令峻弟逸領峻部曲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned him as Grand Minister of Agriculture and ordered Jun's younger brother Yi to lead Jun's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore summoned Jun to court as Grand Minister of Agriculture and ordered Jun's younger brother Yi to command his troops.

sentences.zh: 徵書至，峻怒曰：「庾亮專擅，欲誘殺我也。」

translations.literal: When the summons arrived, Jun angrily said: 'Yu Liang monopolizes power and wishes to lure and kill me.'
translations.idiomatic: When the summons arrived, Jun raged, "Yu Liang monopolizes power and means to lure me to my death."

sentences.zh: 阜陵令匡術、樂安人任讓並為峻謀主，勸峻誅亮。

translations.literal: Fuling Magistrate Kuang Shu and Le'an man Ren Rang both were Jun's chief plotters and urged Jun to execute Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling Magistrate Kuang Shu and a man of Le'an, Ren Rang, were Jun's chief advisers and urged him to kill Liang.

sentences.zh: 乃使使推崇祖約，共討亮，約大喜。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to exalt Zu Yue and jointly attack Liang; Yue was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jun then sent envoys to honor Zu Yue and join him in attacking Liang. Yue was delighted.

sentences.zh: 於是約命兄逖子沛國內史渙、女壻淮南太守許柳將兵會峻。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue ordered his elder brother Di's son, Interior Minister of Peiguo Huan, and his son-in-law Administrator of Huainan Xu Liu to lead troops to join Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then ordered his elder brother Di's son, Interior Minister of Peiguo Huan, and his son-in-law, Administrator of Huainan Xu Liu, to lead troops to join Jun.

sentences.zh: 峻使其黨韓光，光名犯恭宗廟諱，入姑熟，殺于湖令陶馥，殘掠而還。

translations.literal: Jun sent his partisan Han Guang—Guang's name violated the taboo of the temple name of Emperor Gongzong—into Gushu, killed Yuhu Magistrate Tao Fu, plundered savagely, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent his partisan Han Guang—whose name violated the taboo of Emperor Gongzong's temple name—into Gushu, killed Yuhu Magistrate Tao Fu, plundered the region, and returned.

sentences.zh: 衍假庾亮節為征討都督，使其右衞將軍趙胤、左將軍司馬流率眾次于慈湖。

translations.literal: Yan provisionally gave Yu Liang credentials as Commander-in-Chief for punitive expedition and ordered his General of the Right Guard Zhao Yin and General of the Left Sima Liu to lead masses and encamp at Cihu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan gave Yu Liang credentials as punitive expedition commander and ordered his General of the Right Guard Zhao Yin and General of the Left Sima Liu to encamp at Cihu.

sentences.zh: 韓光晨襲流，殺之。

translations.literal: Han Guang raided Liu at dawn and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guang raided Liu at dawn and killed him.

sentences.zh: 衍以其驍騎將軍鍾雅為前鋒監軍，假節，率舟軍拒峻。

translations.literal: Yan made his General of Valiant Cavalry Zhong Ya vanguard supervising general with provisional credentials and ordered him to lead the river army to resist Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan appointed his General of Valiant Cavalry Zhong Ya vanguard supervising general with provisional credentials and ordered him to lead the river fleet against Jun.

sentences.zh: 宣城內史桓彝統吏士次于蕪湖，韓光敗之，大掠宣城諸縣而還。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Xuancheng Huan Yi commanded clerks and soldiers and encamped at Wuhu; Han Guang defeated him, plundered greatly the counties of Xuancheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Minister of Xuancheng Huan Yi encamped at Wuhu with his officials and troops. Han Guang defeated him, plundered the counties of Xuancheng, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史溫嶠使督護王愆期、西陽太守鄧岱、鄱陽太守紀睦等以舟軍赴于建業。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Wen Jiao sent Protector Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Dai, Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu, and others with the river army to hasten to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jiangzhou Wen Jiao sent Protector Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Xiyang Deng Dai, Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu, and others with a river fleet toward Jianye.

sentences.zh: 愆期、岱次直瀆，峻督眾二萬濟自橫江，登牛渚山。

translations.literal: Yanqi and Dai encamped at Zhidu; Jun commanded masses of twenty thousand, crossed from Hengjiang, and ascended Niuzhu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi and Dai encamped at Zhidu. Jun led twenty thousand men across from Hengjiang and ascended Niuzhu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 愆期等邀擊不制。

translations.literal: Yanqi and others intercepted and struck but could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi and the others intercepted them but could not stop the advance.

sentences.zh: 峻至于蔣山，衍假領軍卞壼節，率諸將陳兵。

translations.literal: Jun reached Jiangshan; Yan provisionally gave Leader of the Army Bian Huai credentials and ordered him to lead the generals in deploying troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached Jiangshan, Yan gave Leader of the Army Bian Huai credentials and ordered the generals to deploy their troops.

sentences.zh: 衍之將怯兵弱，為峻所敗，卞壼及其二子、丹陽尹羊曼、黃門侍郎周導、廬江太守陶瞻、散騎侍郎任台等皆死，死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: Yan's generals were timid and troops weak; they were defeated by Jun. Bian Huai and his two sons, Intendant of Danyang Yang Man, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates Zhou Dao, Administrator of Lujiang Tao Zhan, Gentleman Cavalier Attendant Ren Tai, and others all died; the dead exceeded three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's generals were timid and his troops weak. Jun defeated them. Bian Huai and his two sons, Intendant of Danyang Yang Man, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates Zhou Dao, Administrator of Lujiang Tao Zhan, Gentleman Cavalier Attendant Ren Tai, and others were killed—more than three thousand dead in all.

sentences.zh: 庾亮兵敗，與三弟奔于柴桑。

translations.literal: Yu Liang's army was defeated; with his three younger brothers he fled to Chaisang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang's army was defeated, and he fled with his three younger brothers to Chaisang.

sentences.zh: 峻遂焚衍宮，羣賊突掠，百僚奔散，唯有米數石而已，無以自供。

translations.literal: Jun then burned Yan's palace; the bandit masses burst forth in plunder; the hundred officials scattered in flight; there were only several piculs of rice, nothing with which to supply themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jun then burned Yan's palace. The rebel bands looted everywhere, and the officials scattered. Only a few piculs of rice remained—nothing with which to sustain themselves.

sentences.zh: 峻逼衍大赦，庾亮兄弟不在赦限。

translations.literal: Jun compelled Yan to grant a great amnesty; Yu Liang and his brothers were not within the amnesty limits.
translations.idiomatic: Jun forced Yan to issue a general amnesty, but Yu Liang and his brothers were excluded.

sentences.zh: 峻以祖約為太尉、尚書令，加侍中，自為驃騎將軍、領軍將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Jun made Zu Yue Grand Commandant and Master of Writing, with added Palace Attendant; he himself was General of Agile Cavalry, Leader of the Army, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Zu Yue Grand Commandant and Master of Writing with the added title of Palace Attendant. He himself took the posts of General of Agile Cavalry, Leader of the Army, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 於是建業荒毀，奔投吳會者十八九。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jianye was desolate and ruined; eight or nine in ten fled to Wu and Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye was left desolate and ruined; eight or nine households in ten fled toward Wu and Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠聞之，移告征鎮州郡。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao heard of it and sent notices to the expeditionary garrisons, provinces, and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Jiao heard of it, he sent notices to the expeditionary garrisons and provincial commanderies.

sentences.zh: 庾亮至盆口，嶠分兵配給。

translations.literal: Yu Liang reached Penkou; Jiao divided troops and allotted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Liang reached Penkou, Jiao allotted him a share of the troops.

sentences.zh: 又招衍荊州刺史陶侃欲共討峻。

translations.literal: He also recruited Yan's Inspector of Jingzhou Tao Kan, wishing jointly to attack Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He also tried to recruit Yan's Inspector of Jingzhou Tao Kan for a joint campaign against Jun.

sentences.zh: 侃不從，曰：「吾疆埸外將，本非顧命大臣，今日之事，所不敢當。」

translations.literal: Kan did not follow and said: 'I am a frontier general beyond the borders; I was never a entrusted minister at deathbed; today's affair—I dare not undertake it.'
translations.idiomatic: Kan refused, saying, "I am a frontier general beyond the borders, not a deathbed entrusted minister. I dare not take on today's affair."

sentences.zh: 時侃子為峻所害，嶠復喻侃曰：「蘇峻遂得志，四海雖廣，公寧有容足地乎？

translations.literal: At that time Kan's son had been killed by Jun; Jiao again persuaded Kan: 'Su Jun has thus attained his aim; though the four seas are broad, can my lord still have ground enough to set foot?
translations.idiomatic: By then Jun had killed Kan's son. Jiao urged him again, "If Su Jun has his way, though the four seas are vast, will you still have room to set foot anywhere?

sentences.zh: 賢子越騎酷沒，天下為公痛心，況慈父之情哉！」

translations.literal: Your worthy son of the Flying Cavalry suffered cruel death; the realm grieves for my lord—how much more a father's affection!'
translations.idiomatic: Your worthy son of the Flying Cavalry suffered a cruel death. The realm grieves for you—how much more must a father's heart!"

sentences.zh: 侃乃許之。

translations.literal: Kan then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Kan then agreed.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻屯於于湖。

translations.literal: Su Jun encamped at Yuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun encamped at Yuhu.

sentences.zh: 衍母庾氏憂怖而死。

translations.literal: Yan's mother, the Lady Yu, died of worry and terror.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's mother, Lady Yu, died of grief and fear.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻聞兵起，自姑熟還建業，屯于石頭。

translations.literal: Su Jun heard troops had risen, returned from Gushu to Jianye, and encamped at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun heard that troops had risen against him, he returned from Gushu to Jianye and encamped at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 使其黨張瑾、管商率眾拒諸軍，逼遷衍於石頭。

translations.literal: He sent his partisans Zhang Jin and Guan Shang to lead masses to resist the various armies and compelled Yan to move to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his partisans Zhang Jin and Guan Shang to resist the allied armies and forced Yan to move to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 衍哀泣升車，宮人盡哭，隨從衍者，莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Yan wept in grief as he mounted the carriage; palace women all wept; those following Yan—none did not shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yan wept as he mounted the carriage. The palace women all wept, and none of those who followed him could hold back tears.

sentences.zh: 峻以倉屋為宮，使鄉人許方為司馬，督將兵守衞。

translations.literal: Jun used granary buildings as a palace, made his fellow townsman Xu Fang Major, and supervised generals and troops in guard and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made granary buildings his palace, appointed his fellow townsman Xu Fang Major, and set him to command the guard troops.

sentences.zh: 陶侃、庾亮、溫嶠率舟軍二萬至于石頭，俄引還，次于蔡洲沙門浦。

translations.literal: Tao Kan, Yu Liang, and Wen Jiao led a river army of twenty thousand to Shitou, soon withdrew, and encamped at Cai Isle, Shamen Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan, Yu Liang, and Wen Jiao led a fleet of twenty thousand to Shitou, then withdrew and encamped at Shamen Ford on Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 庾亮守白石壘，詰朝，峻將萬餘人攻之。

translations.literal: Yu Liang defended the White Stone rampart; at dawn the next day Jun led more than ten thousand to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang held the White Stone rampart. At dawn the next day Jun attacked with more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 亮等逆擊，峻退。

translations.literal: Liang and others struck in counterattack; Jun retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and the others counterattacked, and Jun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史庾冰率三吳之眾驟戰，不勝。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Wu Yu Bing led the masses of the Three Wu in sudden battle and did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Minister of Wu Yu Bing led the armies of the Three Wu in a sudden battle but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 瑾、商等破庾冰前軍於無錫，焚掠肆意。

translations.literal: Jin, Shang, and others defeated Yu Bing's vanguard at Wuxi and burned and plundered at will.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Shang, and the others defeated Yu Bing's vanguard at Wuxi and burned and plundered at will.

sentences.zh: 韓光攻宣城內史桓彝，彝率吏民力戰不勝，為光所殺。

translations.literal: Han Guang attacked Interior Minister of Xuancheng Huan Yi; Yi led clerks and people in strenuous battle but did not prevail and was killed by Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guang attacked Interior Minister of Xuancheng Huan Yi. Yi led officials and commoners in a desperate fight but was defeated and killed by Guang.

sentences.zh: 祖約為潁川人陳光率其屬攻之，約乃奔於歷陽。

translations.literal: Zu Yue was attacked by Yingchuan man Chen Guang leading his followers; Yue then fled to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue was attacked by Chen Guang of Yingchuan leading his followers, and fled to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 長樂人賈寧勸峻殺王導，盡誅諸大臣，峻不從，乃改計叛峻。

translations.literal: Changle man Jia Ning urged Jun to kill Wang Dao and execute all the great ministers; Jun did not follow, and Ning then changed his plan and rebelled against Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ning of Changle urged Jun to kill Wang Dao and execute all the great ministers. Jun refused, so Ning changed his plan and turned against Jun.

sentences.zh: 王導使袁耽潛誘納之，謀奉衍出奔溫嶠。

translations.literal: Wang Dao sent Yuan Dan to entice and win him over in secret, plotting to support Yan in fleeing to join Wen Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao sent Yuan Dan to win him over in secret, plotting to escort Yan out to join Wen Jiao.

sentences.zh: 嶠食盡，貸于陶侃。

translations.literal: Jiao's food was exhausted; he borrowed from Tao Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's provisions ran out, and he borrowed grain from Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 侃怒曰：「使君前云不憂無士眾及糧食也，唯欲得老民為主耳。

translations.literal: Kan angrily said: 'My lord earlier said you did not worry about lacking soldiers and grain, only wished to have this old commoner as master.
translations.idiomatic: Kan raged, "You said earlier that you had no worry about troops or grain—you only wanted this old man as your leader.

sentences.zh: 今比戰皆北，良將安在？

translations.literal: Now in successive battles all have been defeated—where are the good generals?
translations.idiomatic: Now battle after battle ends in defeat—where are your good generals?

sentences.zh: 今若無食，民便欲西歸。」

translations.literal: Now if there is no food, the people will wish to return west.'
translations.idiomatic: If there is no food now, the people will want to march west and go home."

sentences.zh: 先是嶠慮侃不赴，故以甘言招侃。

translations.literal: Earlier Jiao had worried Kan would not come, and therefore used sweet words to recruit Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiao had feared Kan would not come, and had therefore wooed him with flattering words.

sentences.zh: 嶠乃卑辭謝之，且曰：「今者，騎虎之勢可得下乎？

translations.literal: Jiao then used humble words to apologize and also said: 'Now, can one dismount from the tiger's back?
translations.idiomatic: Jiao then apologized humbly and said, "Can one now climb down from a tiger's back?

sentences.zh: 賊垂滅，願公留思。」

translations.literal: The bandits are nearly destroyed; I wish my lord would keep this in mind.'
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are nearly destroyed. I beg you to consider that."

sentences.zh: 侃怒少止。

translations.literal: Kan's anger somewhat ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's anger subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 其將李陽說曰：「今事若不捷，雖有粟，焉得而食之。

translations.literal: His general Li Yang urged: 'If today's affair does not succeed, though there is grain, how could one eat it?
translations.idiomatic: His general Li Yang urged, "If today's campaign fails, grain will do us no good.

sentences.zh: 公宜割見儲，以卒大事。」

translations.literal: My lord should cut from visible stores to complete the great affair.'
translations.idiomatic: You should draw on your stores now to finish the great affair."

sentences.zh: 乃以米五萬石供軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he supplied the army with fifty thousand piculs of rice.
translations.idiomatic: He then supplied the army with fifty thousand piculs of rice.

sentences.zh: 祖渙襲湓口，欲以沮溫嶠之兵。

translations.literal: Zu Huan raided Penkou, wishing to obstruct Wen Jiao's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Huan raided Penkou, hoping to obstruct Wen Jiao's army.

sentences.zh: 渙過晥，攻譙國內史桓雲，不克，乃還。

translations.literal: Huan passed Wan, attacked Interior Minister of Qiao Huan Yun, did not overcome him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huan passed through Wan, attacked Interior Minister of Qiao Huan Yun, failed to take him, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻并兵攻大業，大業水竭，皆飲糞汁。

translations.literal: Su Jun combined troops to attack Daye; Daye's water was exhausted, and all drank filth-water.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun concentrated his forces against Daye. When Daye's water ran out, the defenders drank filthy water.

sentences.zh: 諸將謀救之，慮不能當，且欲水陸攻峻。

translations.literal: The generals plotted to rescue it, worried they could not withstand him, and also wished to attack Jun by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: The generals planned a rescue but feared they could not hold Jun off, and also considered a combined land-and-water attack.

sentences.zh: 陶侃以舟師攻石頭，溫嶠、庾亮陳于白石。

translations.literal: Tao Kan with the river army attacked Shitou; Wen Jiao and Yu Liang deployed at White Stone.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan attacked Shitou with the fleet while Wen Jiao and Yu Liang deployed at White Stone.

sentences.zh: 峻子碩以數十騎出戰，峻見碩騎，乃捨其眾，自以四馬北下突陳，[6]陳堅乃還。

translations.literal: Jun's son Shuo went out to battle with several tens of horsemen; Jun saw Shuo's horsemen, then abandoned his masses, himself with four horses charged north down into the formation, [6] the formation was firm and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Shuo rode out with several dozen horsemen. When Jun saw Shuo's riders, he abandoned his main force and charged the enemy line with four horses. [6] The line held firm, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 軍士彭世、李千投之以矛，峻墜馬，遂梟首，臠割之，焚其骸骨。

translations.literal: Soldiers Peng Shi and Li Qian cast spears at him; Jun fell from his horse; they then displayed his head, carved his flesh, and burned his bones.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers Peng Shi and Li Qian hurled spears at him. Jun fell from his horse. They displayed his head, carved up his flesh, and burned his bones.

sentences.zh: 任讓及諸賊帥復立峻弟逸，求峻屍弗獲，乃發衍父母冢，[7]剖棺焚屍。

translations.literal: Ren Rang and the various bandit chiefs again installed Jun's younger brother Yi; seeking Jun's corpse they did not obtain it; thereupon they opened Yan's parents' tomb, [7] split the coffin and burned the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Rang and the rebel chiefs installed Jun's younger brother Yi. Unable to find Jun's body, they opened Yan's parents' tomb [7] and burned the corpses.

sentences.zh: 匡術率其徒據苑城以降，韓光、蘇碩等率眾攻苑，苑中飢，穀石四萬。

translations.literal: Kuang Shu led his followers to hold Yuan city and surrender; Han Guang, Su Shuo, and others led masses to attack Yuan; in Yuan there was famine, grain four ten-thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Shu held Yuan city with his followers and surrendered. Han Guang, Su Shuo, and others attacked Yuan. The city was starving, though grain was priced at forty thousand per picul.

sentences.zh: 諸將攻石頭。

translations.literal: The generals attacked Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: The generals attacked Shitou.

sentences.zh: 蘇碩及章武王世子休率勁賊孔盧、張偏等數十人擊李陽於柤浦，退走，碩等追之，庾冰司馬滕含以銳卒自後擊之，碩、逸等震潰，奔于曲阿。

translations.literal: Su Shuo and the Heir of Prince Zhangwu Xiu led fierce bandits Kong Lu, Zhang Pian, and several tens of men to strike Li Yang at Zhapu; they retreated and fled; Shuo and others pursued; Yu Bing's Major Teng Han with sharp troops struck from the rear; Shuo, Yi, and others were shaken and routed and fled to Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shuo and the Heir of Prince Zhangwu Xiu led fierce rebels Kong Lu, Zhang Pian, and several dozen men against Li Yang at Zhapu. They retreated, but Shuo pursued them. Yu Bing's Major Teng Han struck from the rear with elite troops, routing Shuo, Yi, and the others, who fled to Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 含入抱衍，始得出奔溫嶠之舟。

translations.literal: Han entered, embraced Yan, and only then was able to flee out to Wen Jiao's boats.
translations.idiomatic: Han entered the palace, embraced Yan, and only then was able to flee to Wen Jiao's boats.

sentences.zh: 是時，兵破之後，宮室灰燼，議欲遷移，王導不從乃止。

translations.literal: At this time, after the armies were broken, the palaces were ashes; they debated moving the capital; Wang Dao did not follow and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: After the armies were broken, the palaces lay in ashes. Some debated moving the capital, but Wang Dao opposed it and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 衍改年咸康。

translations.literal: Yan changed the era to Xiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan changed the era name to Xiankang.

sentences.zh: 建國中，衍死。

translations.literal: In Jianguo, Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianguo period, Yan died.

sentences.zh: 中書監庾冰廢衍子千齡，立其弟岳，改年曰建元。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Supervisor Yu Bing deposed Yan's son Qianling and installed his younger brother Yue, changing the era to Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Supervisor Yu Bing deposed Yan's son Qianling and installed his younger brother Yue, changing the era name to Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 初岳之立，當改元，庾冰立號，而晉初已有，改作，又如之，乃為建元。

translations.literal: When Yue was first installed, the era should have been changed; Yu Bing established a title, but Jinyuan already existed at the beginning of Jin; he changed it, then again did so, and thus made Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue first took the throne, the era name was due to be changed. Yu Bing proposed a title, but Jinyuan had already been used early in the Jin dynasty. He revised it once, then again, and settled on Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，或告冰曰：「子作年號，乃不視讖也。

translations.literal: Soon someone told Bing: 'You made an era name without heeding the prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone told Bing, "You chose an era name without heeding the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 讖云：『建元之末丘山崩。』

translations.literal: The prophecy says: 'At the end of Jianyuan the hill-mountain collapses.'
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy says, "At the end of Jianyuan the hill-mountain collapses."

sentences.zh: 丘山，岳也。」

translations.literal: Hill-mountain' is Yue.'
translations.idiomatic: Hill-mountain" means Yue."

sentences.zh: 冰瞿然，久而歎曰：「如有吉凶，豈改易所能救乎？」

translations.literal: Bing was startled; after a long while he sighed: 'If there is fortune or misfortune, how could changing and altering save it?'
translations.idiomatic: Bing was startled. After a long pause he sighed, "If fortune or misfortune is fated, how could changing the name save us?"

sentences.zh: 遂不復改。

translations.literal: He then did not change it again.
translations.idiomatic: He did not change it again.

sentences.zh: 岳死，庾冰欲立司馬昱。

translations.literal: Yue died; Yu Bing wished to install Sima Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue died, Yu Bing wished to install Sima Yu.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍何充立岳子聃，號年曰永和。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry He Chong installed Yue's son Dan and styled the era Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry He Chong installed Yue's son Dan and styled the era Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 聃安西將軍桓溫率所統七千餘人伐蜀，拜表輒行。

translations.literal: Dan's General Who Pacifies the West Huan Wen led more than seven thousand of his command to attack Shu, memorialized and at once marched.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's General Who Pacifies the West Huan Wen led more than seven thousand of his troops to attack Shu and marched as soon as his memorial was sent.

sentences.zh: 聃威力微弱，不能控制也。

translations.literal: Dan's power and prestige were slight; he could not control Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's authority was too weak to control him.

sentences.zh: 及石虎死，聃征北將軍褚裒以舟軍至下邳，西中郎將陳逵進據淮南。

translations.literal: When Shi Hu died, Dan's General Who Campaigns North Chu Pou led a river army to Xiapi; Western Central Commander Chen Kui advanced and held Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu died, Dan's General Who Campaigns North Chu Pou led a river fleet to Xiapi, and Western Central Commander Chen Kui advanced into Huainan.

sentences.zh: 石遵聞裒至下邳，使其司空李農領萬餘騎逆圍督護王龕於薛，執龕送于鄴，又殺李邁。

translations.literal: Shi Zun heard Pou had reached Xiapi and sent his Minister of Works Li Nong leading more than ten thousand horsemen to meet and besiege Protector Wang Kan at Xue, seized Kan and sent him to Ye, and also killed Li Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun heard Pou had reached Xiapi and sent his Minister of Works Li Nong with more than ten thousand horsemen to besiege Protector Wang Kan at Xue. Kan was seized and sent to Ye, and Li Mai was also killed.

sentences.zh: 龕，裒之驍將，三軍喪氣，乃引還。

translations.literal: Kan was Pou's fierce general; the Three Armies lost spirit and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was Pou's best general. The army lost heart and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 陳逵聞之，震懼，焚淮南而走。

translations.literal: Chen Kui heard of it, was shaken and afraid, burned Huainan, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Kui heard of it, he was terrified, burned Huainan, and fled.

sentences.zh: 桓溫表廢聃揚州刺史殷浩，聃憚溫，乃除其名。

translations.literal: Huan Wen memorialized to depose Dan's Inspector of Yangzhou Yin Hao; Dan feared Wen and removed Hao's name from office.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen memorialized to depose Dan's Inspector of Yangzhou Yin Hao. Dan feared Wen and removed Hao from office.

sentences.zh: 溫遂率所統諸軍步騎四萬自郢越關中至灞上。

translations.literal: Wen then led all his armies, forty thousand foot and horse, from Ying across the passes of Guanzhong to Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then led forty thousand foot and horse from his command out of Ying, across the Guanzhong passes to Bashang.

sentences.zh: 苻健與五千餘人守長安小城。

translations.literal: Fu Jian with more than five thousand men defended the small city of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian defended the small city of Chang'an with more than five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是歲大儉，溫軍人懸磐，健深溝堅壁，清野待溫。

translations.literal: That year there was great famine; Wen's army men were in dire want; Jian dug deep moats and strengthened walls, cleared the countryside, and awaited Wen.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought great famine. Wen's troops were starving. Jian dug deep moats, strengthened his walls, cleared the countryside, and waited for Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫軍食盡，乃退，苻健遣子萇頻擊敗之。

translations.literal: Wen's army's food was exhausted and he withdrew; Fu Jian sent his son Chang repeatedly to strike and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen's provisions ran out, he withdrew. Fu Jian sent his son Chang repeatedly to strike and defeat him.

sentences.zh: 初，溫次灞上，其部將振武將軍、順陽太守薛珍勸溫徑進逼城，溫弗從，珍以偏師獨濟，頗有所獲。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wen halted at Bashang, his subordinate General Who Quells Martial Ferocity, Administrator of Shunyang Xue Zhen urged Wen to advance straight and press the city; Wen did not follow; Zhen with a detached force crossed alone and gained somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wen halted at Bashang, his subordinate General Who Quells Martial Ferocity, Administrator of Shunyang Xue Zhen urged him to press straight against the city. Wen refused. Zhen crossed with a detached force on his own and gained some booty.

sentences.zh: 溫退，珍乃還，放言於眾，且矜其銳而咎溫之持重。

translations.literal: When Wen withdrew, Zhen then returned, spread words among the masses, and both boasted of his sharpness and blamed Wen's caution.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen withdrew, Zhen returned and boasted among the troops of his boldness while blaming Wen's caution.

sentences.zh: 溫慚忿，殺之。

translations.literal: Wen was ashamed and angry and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, ashamed and furious, had him killed.

sentences.zh: 聃又改年曰升平。

translations.literal: Dan again changed the era to Shengping.
translations.idiomatic: Dan again changed the era name to Shengping.

sentences.zh: 聃死，無子，立衍子丕，號年隆和。

translations.literal: Dan died without sons; they installed Yan's son Pi and styled the era Longhe.
translations.idiomatic: Dan died without sons. They installed Yan's son Pi and styled the era Longhe.

sentences.zh: 時謠曰：「升平不滿斗，隆和那得久。」

translations.literal: At the time a rhyme said: 'Shengping does not fill a dipper; Longhe—how could it last long?'
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme of the time said, "Shengping does not fill a dipper; Longhe—how could it last long?"

sentences.zh: 改為興寧，又謠曰：「雖復改興寧，亦自無聊生。」

translations.literal: It was changed to Xingning; again a rhyme said: 'Though you change again to Xingning, still there is no way to live.'
translations.idiomatic: The era was changed to Xingning, and another rhyme said, "Though you change again to Xingning, still there is no way to live."

sentences.zh: 丕死，弟弈立，號年曰太和。

translations.literal: Pi died; his younger brother Yi was installed and the era styled Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi died, his younger brother Yi was installed and the era styled Taihe.

sentences.zh: 桓溫率眾北討慕容暐，至金鄉，鑿鉅野三百餘里以通舟軍，自清水入河。

translations.literal: Huan Wen led masses north to attack Murong Wei, reached Jinxiang, cut through Juye more than three hundred li to open a passage for the river army, and from Qingshui entered the river.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen led his army north against Murong Wei. At Jinxiang he cut a channel more than three hundred li through Juye to open a water route for his fleet, entering the river from Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂逆擊破之，獲其資仗。

translations.literal: Murong Chui struck in counterattack and defeated him, seizing his supplies and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui counterattacked and defeated him, seizing his supplies and weapons.

sentences.zh: 溫之北引也，先命西中郎將袁真及趙悅開石門，而袁真等停於梁宋，石門不通，糧竭。

translations.literal: When Wen marched north, he first ordered Western Central Commander Yuan Zhen and Zhao Yue to open Shimen, but Yuan Zhen and others halted in Liang and Song; Shimen did not open and grain was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen marched north, he first ordered Western Central Commander Yuan Zhen and Zhao Yue to open Shimen. Yuan Zhen halted in Liang and Song, Shimen never opened, and the army's grain ran out.

sentences.zh: 溫自枋頭回軍，垂以步騎數萬追及襄邑，大敗溫軍。

translations.literal: Wen withdrew his army from Fangtou; Chui with several tens of thousands of foot and horse pursued to Xiangyi and utterly defeated Wen's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wen withdrew from Fangtou. Chui pursued with tens of thousands of foot and horse to Xiangyi and routed Wen's army.

sentences.zh: 溫遂歸罪袁真，除名削爵，收節傳。

translations.literal: Wen then placed blame on Yuan Zhen, removed his name and stripped his title, and seized his credentials and commission.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then blamed Yuan Zhen, stripped his name and title, and seized his credentials and commission.

sentences.zh: 真子雙之等殺梁國內史朱憲，真據壽陽以叛，真諸子兄弟阻兵自守，招誘陸城戍將陳郡太守朱輔數千人。

translations.literal: Zhen's son Shuangzhi and others killed Interior Minister of Liang Zhu Xian; Zhen held Shouyang and rebelled; Zhen's sons and brothers blocked troops and defended themselves, enticing the garrison commander of Lucheng, Administrator of Chen Zhu Fu, with several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's son Shuangzhi and others killed Interior Minister of Liang Zhu Xian. Zhen held Shouyang in rebellion. His sons and brothers took up arms in defense and won over the garrison commander of Lucheng, Administrator of Chen Zhu Fu, with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍爨亮通慕容暐，又遣使西降苻堅。

translations.literal: He sent Adjutant Cuan Liang to communicate with Murong Wei and also sent envoys west to submit to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Adjutant Cuan Liang to communicate with Murong Wei and also sent envoys west to submit to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 真病死，輔立其嫡子瑾為使持節、建威將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhen died of illness; Fu installed his legitimate son Jin as Bearer of Staff and Credentials, General Who Establishes Might, and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen died of illness, Fu installed his legitimate son Jin as Bearer of Staff and Credentials, General Who Establishes Might, and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑾弟四五人皆領兵。

translations.literal: Jin's four or five younger brothers all commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's four or five younger brothers all commanded troops.

sentences.zh: 暐令陳文報爨亮，且以觀變。

translations.literal: Wei ordered Chen Wen to reply to Cuan Liang and also to observe how affairs changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ordered Chen Wen to reply to Cuan Liang and to watch how affairs developed.

sentences.zh: 桓溫遣督護竺瑤以軍泝淮伐瑾，瑤次于肥口，屢戰。

translations.literal: Huan Wen sent Protector Zhu Yao with an army up the Huai to attack Jin; Yao encamped at Feikou and fought repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen sent Protector Zhu Yao up the Huai to attack Jin. Yao encamped at Feikou and fought repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐假瑾征南將軍、揚州刺史、宣城公，瑾弟泓等皆郡守、四品將軍，朱輔亦如之。

translations.literal: Murong Wei provisionally made Jin General Who Campaigns South, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Duke of Xuancheng; Jin's younger brothers Hong and others were all commandery administrators and fourth-rank generals; Zhu Fu was likewise.
