translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei appointed Jin Acting General Who Campaigns South, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Duke of Xuancheng. Jin's younger brothers Hong and others became commandery administrators and fourth-rank generals, and Zhu Fu received similar honors.

sentences.zh: 溫乃伐瑾，瑾等拒戰，於是築長圍守之，城中震潰，遂平瑾。

translations.literal: Wen then attacked Jin; Jin and others resisted in battle; thereupon he built a long encirclement and besieged them; within the city they were shaken and routed, and Jin was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then attacked Jin. Jin resisted, but Wen built a long encirclement and besieged the city until it collapsed in panic. Jin was pacified.

sentences.zh: 初溫任兼將相，其不臣之心，形于音氣，曾臥對親僚，撫枕而起曰：「為爾寂寂，將為文、景所笑。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wen held both general and minister posts, his unministerial heart showed in voice and bearing; once lying down facing close colleagues, he stroked the pillow and rose, saying: 'For you I remain obscure—Wen and Jing will laugh at me.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wen held both military and civil power, his disloyal intent showed in voice and bearing. Once, lying among close colleagues, he stroked his pillow and rose, saying, "For your sake I remain obscure—Emperors Wen and Jing would laugh at me."

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: The assembly dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared reply.

sentences.zh: 後悉眾北討，冀成陵奪之勢。

translations.literal: Later he led all his forces in northern campaign, hoping to achieve the momentum of usurping the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he led all his forces on the northern campaign, hoping to achieve the momentum of usurping imperial power.

sentences.zh: 及枋頭奔敗，知民望之去己，既平瑾，問中書郎郗超曰：「足以雪枋頭之耻乎？」

translations.literal: When he fled in defeat from Fangtou, he knew popular expectation had left him; after pacifying Jin, he asked Palace Attendant Xi Chao: 'Is it enough to wash away the shame of Fangtou?'
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Fangtou, he knew popular expectation had turned from him. After pacifying Jin, he asked Palace Attendant Xi Chao, "Is this enough to wash away the shame of Fangtou?"

sentences.zh: 超曰：「此未厭有識之情也。

translations.literal: Chao said: 'This does not yet satisfy the feelings of those with understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "This does not yet satisfy men of discernment.

sentences.zh: 公六十之年，敗於大舉，不建不世之勳，不足以鎮愜民望。」

translations.literal: My lord, in your sixtieth year, defeated in a great campaign—if you do not establish an unworldly merit, it is not enough to settle and satisfy popular expectation.'
translations.idiomatic: At sixty, after defeat in a great campaign, you must establish an unworldly achievement if you are to satisfy popular expectation."

sentences.zh: 因說溫以廢立之事。

translations.literal: He then urged Wen with the matter of deposing and installing.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged Wen toward deposing and installing the emperor.

sentences.zh: 溫既宿有此謀，深納超言。

translations.literal: Wen had long harbored this plot and deeply accepted Chao's words.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had long harbored this design and deeply accepted Chao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 溫自廣陵將旋鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: Wen was about to return from Guangling to garrison Guniu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was returning from Guangling to garrison Guniu.

sentences.zh: 至于白石，及言其主弈少同閹人之疾，初在東海、琅邪國，親近嬖人相龍、朱靈寶等並侍臥內，而美人田氏、孟氏遂生三男。

translations.literal: Reaching Baishi, he spoke of how his lord Yi in youth shared the affliction of eunuchs; at first in the states of Donghai and Langye, close favorites Xiang Long, Zhu Lingbao, and others all attended within the bedchamber, while beauties Lady Tian and Lady Meng then bore three sons.
translations.idiomatic: At Baishi he spoke of how his lord Yi in youth had shared the afflictions of eunuchs. In Donghai and Langye he had kept favorites Xiang Long, Zhu Lingbao, and others in his bedchamber, while Ladies Tian and Meng bore three sons.

sentences.zh: 眾致疑惑，然莫能審其虛實。

translations.literal: The masses raised doubts, yet none could examine whether it was false or true.
translations.idiomatic: The court raised doubts, but none could determine the truth.

sentences.zh: 至是，將建儲立王，溫因之以定廢立之計。

translations.literal: At this point, as they were about to establish an heir and install a king, Wen used it to fix his plan of deposition and installation.
translations.idiomatic: As the court was about to establish an heir, Wen used the occasion to fix his plan of deposition and installation.

sentences.zh: 遂率百僚並還朝堂。

translations.literal: He then led the hundred officials together back to the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the officials back to the court hall.

sentences.zh: 溫率眾入，屯兵宮門，進坐殿庭，使督謢竺瑤、散騎侍郎劉亨取弈璽綬。

translations.literal: Wen led masses in, encamped troops at the palace gates, advanced and sat in the hall courtyard, and sent Protector Zhu Yao and Gentleman Cavalier Attendant Liu Heng to take Yi's seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Wen led his troops in, encamped at the palace gates, entered and sat in the hall courtyard, and sent Protector Zhu Yao and Gentleman Cavalier Attendant Liu Heng to take Yi's seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 弈著白袷單衣，步下西堂，登犢車。

translations.literal: Yi wore a white lined single garment, walked down from the western hall, and mounted a ox-cart.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wore a white lined single garment, walked down from the western hall, and mounted an ox-cart.

sentences.zh: 羣臣拜辭，皆殞涕。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers bowed in farewell; all shed tears to death.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers bowed in farewell, all in tears.

sentences.zh: 侍御史將百餘人，送出神虎門，入東海第。

translations.literal: Attending censors with more than a hundred men escorted him out through the Divine Tiger Gate into the Donghai residence.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred attending censors escorted him out through the Divine Tiger Gate to the Donghai residence.

sentences.zh: 於是迎司馬昱而立之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they welcomed Sima Yu and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: They then welcomed Sima Yu and installed him.

sentences.zh: 昱，叡子也。

translations.literal: Yu was Rui's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a son of Rui.

sentences.zh: 昱東向流涕，拜受璽綬。

translations.literal: Yu faced east, weeping, and bowed to receive the seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Yu faced east in tears and bowed to receive the seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 昱既僭立，改年曰咸安，以溫依諸葛亮故事，甲仗入殿，進丞相，其大司馬等皆如故，留鎮建業。

translations.literal: Yu having usurped the throne, changed the era to Xian'an, and following Zhuge Liang's precedent for Wen, allowed arms and armor in the hall, promoted him to Chancellor; his Grand Marshal and other posts remained as before, and he was left to garrison Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu had usurped the throne, he changed the era to Xian'an. Following the precedent of Zhuge Liang, he allowed Wen arms and armor in the hall and promoted him to Chancellor while leaving his other posts unchanged. Wen remained to garrison Jianye.

sentences.zh: 以弈為海西縣公。

translations.literal: Yi was made Duke of Haixi County.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was made Duke of Haixi County.

sentences.zh: 溫常有大志，昱心不自安，謂中書郎郗超曰：「命之修短，本所不計，故當無復近日事邪？」

translations.literal: Wen constantly had great ambitions; Yu's heart was not at ease; he said to Palace Attendant Xi Chao: 'The length of life I do not reckon—but surely there will be no more recent affairs?'
translations.idiomatic: Wen constantly harbored great ambitions, and Yu was uneasy. He said to Palace Attendant Xi Chao, "I do not reckon the length of my life—but surely there will be no more recent troubles?"

sentences.zh: 超父愔為會稽太守，超假還東，昱謂之曰：「致意尊公，家國之事，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Chao's father Yin was Administrator of Kuaiji; Chao took leave to return east; Yu said to him: 'Convey my regard to your honored father—the affairs of house and state have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's father Yin was Administrator of Kuaiji. When Chao took leave to return east, Yu said to him, "Convey my regard to your honored father. The affairs of house and state have come to this.

sentences.zh: 由吾不能以道匡衞，思患豫防，愧歎之深，言何能喻！」

translations.literal: Because I could not use the Way to correct and guard, think of calamity and guard beforehand—the depth of shame and sighing, how can words convey it!'
translations.idiomatic: Because I could not uphold the Way and guard against disaster beforehand, my shame and grief are beyond words."

sentences.zh: 又誦庾闡詩云：「志士痛朝危，忠臣哀主辱。」

translations.literal: He also recited Yu Chan's poem: 'Men of resolve grieve when the court is endangered; loyal ministers mourn when the lord is shamed.'
translations.idiomatic: He also recited Yu Chan's lines: "Men of resolve grieve when the court is endangered; loyal ministers mourn when the lord is shamed."

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept.
translations.idiomatic: And he wept.

sentences.zh: 昱疾，與溫書曰：「吾遂委篤，足下便入，冀得相見，不謂疾患，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Yu fell ill and wrote to Wen: 'I am now utterly prostrate; my lord, come in at once—I hoped we might meet, but did not expect illness to reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu fell ill, he wrote to Wen: "I am now utterly prostrate. Come at once—I hoped we might meet, but did not expect my illness to reach this point.

sentences.zh: 今者惙然，勢不復久，且雖有詔，豈復相及。

translations.literal: Now I am feeble; the momentum will not last long; and though there is an edict, how could we still meet.
translations.idiomatic: I am feeble now and will not last long. Even if an edict is sent, how could we still meet?

sentences.zh: 慨恨兼深，如何可言！

translations.literal: Regret and resentment together are deep—how can it be spoken!
translations.idiomatic: My regret and resentment are too deep for words!

sentences.zh: 天下艱難，而昌明幼冲眇然，非阿衡輔導之訓，當何以寧濟也？

translations.literal: The realm is in hardship, yet Changming is young and slight—without the instruction of an Ah Heng to assist and guide, how can there be peace and order?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in hardship, and Changming is young and slight. Without an Ah Heng to assist and guide him, how can there be peace?

sentences.zh: 國事家計，一託於公。」

translations.literal: The affairs of state and household—I entrust all to my lord.'
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of state and household I entrust entirely to you."

sentences.zh: 昱死，子昌明僭立。

translations.literal: Yu died; his son Changming usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu died, his son Changming usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 徐州小吏盧悚與其妖眾男女二百，向晨攻廣莫門，詐言海西公還，由萬春、雲龍門入殿，略取三廂及武庫甲仗。

translations.literal: Xuzhou petty clerk Lu Song with his demonic masses, two hundred men and women, at dawn attacked the Guangmo Gate, falsely claiming the Duke of Haixi had returned; through Wanchun and Yunlong gates they entered the hall, plundered the three wings and the armory's armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: A petty clerk of Xuzhou, Lu Song, with two hundred men and women of his demonic band attacked the Guangmo Gate at dawn, falsely claiming the Duke of Haixi had returned. They entered the hall through the Wanchun and Yunlong gates and plundered the three wings of the palace and the armory.

sentences.zh: 時門下軍校並假兼，在直吏士駭愕不知所為。

translations.literal: At the time the gate guards were all provisional and concurrent; the clerks on duty were shocked and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards were all provisional appointees, and the clerks on duty were too shocked to act.

sentences.zh: 游擊將軍毛安之先入雲龍門討悚，中領軍桓祕、將軍殷康止車門入，會兵攻之，斬五十六級，捕獲餘黨，死者數百人。

translations.literal: Mobile General Mao Anzhi first entered Yunlong Gate to attack Song; Central Leader of the Army Huan Mi and General Yin Kang halted at the carriage gate and entered; they joined forces to attack, beheaded fifty-six heads, captured the remaining partisans, and the dead numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile General Mao Anzhi entered Yunlong Gate first to attack Song. Central Leader of the Army Huan Mi and General Yin Kang entered at the carriage gate. Together they attacked, beheaded fifty-six men, captured the remaining rebels, and left several hundred dead.

sentences.zh: 前殿中監許龍與悚皆遣人至吳，詐迎弈，弈不從。

translations.literal: Former Palace Director Xu Long and Song both sent men to Wu, falsely to welcome Yi; Yi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Former Palace Director Xu Long and Song both sent men to Wu under false pretenses to welcome Yi, but Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 昌明改年曰寧康，[8]徵溫入朝，又詔溫無拜。

translations.literal: Changming changed the era to Ningkang, [8] summoned Wen to court, and also ordered Wen not to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Changming changed the era to Ningkang, [8] summoned Wen to court, and also ordered that Wen need not bow.

sentences.zh: 尚書謝安等於新亭見溫，皆敬。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Xie An and others met Wen at Xinting; all were respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Xie An and others met Wen at Xinting with full respect.

sentences.zh: 溫拜昱墓，得病還姑熟。

translations.literal: Wen paid respects at Yu's tomb, fell ill, and returned to Guniu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen paid his respects at Yu's tomb, fell ill, and returned to Guniu.

sentences.zh: 溫自歸寢疾，諷求備物九錫。

translations.literal: Wen, having returned to nurse his illness, hinted and sought the nine bestowals of full ritual equipment.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to nurse his illness, Wen hinted that he sought the nine bestowals.

sentences.zh: 謝安已令吏部郎袁彥伯撰策文，文成，安輒勾點，令更治改。

translations.literal: Xie An had already ordered Ministry of Personnel Attendant Yuan Yanbo to compose the investiture text; when the text was complete, An at once marked corrections and ordered it revised again.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An had already ordered Ministry of Personnel Attendant Yuan Yanbo to draft the investiture text. When it was finished, An marked corrections and ordered it revised again.

sentences.zh: 既屢引日，乃謀於尚書僕射王彪之，彪之云：「聞彼病日增，亦當不復支久，自可小遲回其事。」

translations.literal: After repeatedly drawing out days, he then plotted with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Biaozhi; Biaozhi said: 'I hear his illness increases daily; he also surely cannot last long—naturally one may slightly delay and turn back this affair.'
translations.idiomatic: After repeatedly drawing out the days, he consulted Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Biaozhi. Biaozhi said, "I hear his illness grows daily. He surely cannot last long. We may safely delay the matter a little."

sentences.zh: 安從之。

translations.literal: An followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An agreed.

sentences.zh: 溫死。

translations.literal: Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: Wen died.

sentences.zh: 是時，昌明年長，嗜酒好內，而昌明弟會稽王道子任居宰相，昏醟尤甚，狎昵諂邪。

translations.literal: At this time Changming was grown, addicted to wine and fond of women; Changming's younger brother the Prince of Kuaiji Daozi held the post of Chancellor, was especially muddled and drunken, and was intimate with flatterers and the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: By then Changming had grown up, addicted to wine and fond of women. His younger brother, the Prince of Kuaiji Daozi, held the chancellorship, was deeply muddled by drink, and kept company with flatterers and the wicked.

sentences.zh: 于時尼娼構扇內外，風俗頹薄，人無廉耻。

translations.literal: At that time nuns and prostitutes stirred faction within and without; customs were decadent and thin; people had no sense of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Nuns and prostitutes stirred faction throughout the court. Customs decayed, and people lost all sense of shame.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王珣兒婚，門客車數百乘，會聞王雅為太子少傅，回以詣雅者半焉。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Xun's son married; client carriages numbered several hundred; it happened that Wang Ya was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and half turned back to visit Ya.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Vice Director Wang Xun's son married, several hundred client carriages attended. Word came that Wang Ya had been made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and half the carriages turned back to visit him instead.

sentences.zh: 雅素有寵，人情去就若此。

translations.literal: Ya had long enjoyed favor; human sentiment shifted thus.
translations.idiomatic: Ya had long enjoyed favor, and human sentiment shifted as swiftly as this.

sentences.zh: 皇始元年，昌明死，子德宗僭立。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangshi, Changming died; his son Dezong usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangshi, Changming died and his son Dezong usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，昌明耽於酒色，末年，殆為長夜之飲，醒治既少，外人罕得接見，故多居內殿，流連於樽俎之間。

translations.literal: Earlier, Changming was addicted to wine and women; in his later years he was almost in an all-night drinking bout; sober governance was already slight; outsiders rarely gained audience; therefore he mostly dwelt in the inner halls, lingering between wine-cups and meat-platters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Changming had been addicted to wine and women. In his later years he drank almost through the night, governed little when sober, and rarely received outsiders. He spent most of his time in the inner halls, lingering over wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 以嬖姬張氏為貴人，寵冠後宮，威行閫內。

translations.literal: He made his favorite Lady Zhang a Noble Lady; her favor crowned the rear palace and her authority extended within the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He made his favorite Lady Zhang a Noble Lady. Her favor crowned the rear palace, and her authority ruled within the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 於時年幾三十，昌明妙列妓樂，陪侍嬪少，乃笑而戲之云：「汝以年當廢，吾已屬諸姝少矣。」

translations.literal: At that time she was nearly thirty; Changming skillfully arrayed courtesans and music; the attending consorts were few; he then laughed and teased her: 'You by age ought to be dismissed—I have already assigned you to the younger beauties.'
translations.idiomatic: She was then nearly thirty. Changming had courtesans and musicians finely arrayed, while few consorts attended him. He laughed and teased her, "By your age you ought to be dismissed. I have already assigned you to the younger beauties."

sentences.zh: 張氏潛怒，昌明不覺而戲逾甚。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang secretly grew angry; Changming did not notice and teased ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang secretly grew angry, but Changming did not notice and teased her ever more.

sentences.zh: 向夕，昌明稍醉，張氏乃多潛飲宦者內侍而分遣焉。

translations.literal: Toward evening Changming was slightly drunk; Lady Zhang then secretly gave many drinks to eunuch attendants and sent them away in groups.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening, when Changming was slightly drunk, Lady Zhang secretly plied the eunuch attendants with wine and sent them away in groups.

sentences.zh: 至暮，昌明沉醉臥，張氏遂令其婢蒙之以被，既絕而懼，貨左右云以魘死。

translations.literal: By dusk Changming was deeply drunk and lay down; Lady Zhang then ordered her maid to cover him with a quilt; when he was dead she feared and bribed those around to say he died of nightmare.
translations.idiomatic: By dusk Changming lay in drunken sleep. Lady Zhang ordered her maid to smother him with a quilt. When he was dead she feared exposure and bribed those around to say he had died of a nightmare.

sentences.zh: 時道子昏廢，子元顯專政，遂不窮張氏之罪。

translations.literal: At the time Daozi was muddled and useless; his son Yuanxian monopolized government; they therefore did not pursue Lady Zhang's crime to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi was muddled and useless, and his son Yuanxian monopolized government. Lady Zhang's crime was never fully pursued.

sentences.zh: 德宗既立，改年為隆安。

translations.literal: Dezong having been installed, changed the era to Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dezong was installed, he changed the era name to Long'an.

sentences.zh: 以道子為太傅、揚州牧、中書監，加殊禮，黃鉞、羽葆、鼓吹，又增甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: Daozi was made Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, and Palace Secretariat Supervisor, with special honors, yellow battle-axe, feather canopy, and ceremonial music, and a further hundred armed guards entering the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi was made Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, and Palace Secretariat Supervisor, with special honors including the yellow battle-axe, feather canopy, and ceremonial music, and a further hundred armed guards were allowed into the hall.

sentences.zh: 既而內外眾事必先關於道子。

translations.literal: Soon all matters within and without had first to pass through Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all matters within and without the court had first to pass through Daozi.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射王國寶輕薄無行，為道子所親，權震建業，擅取東宮兵以配己府。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Guobao was frivolous and without conduct, favored by Daozi; his authority shook Jianye; he seized Eastern Palace troops on his own authority to assign to his own headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Guobao was frivolous and dissolute, favored by Daozi. His authority dominated Jianye, and he seized Eastern Palace troops for his own headquarters.

sentences.zh: 道子以王緒為輔國將軍、琅邪內史，又輒并石頭之兵，屯于建業。

translations.literal: Daozi made Wang Xu General Who Assists the State and Interior Minister of Langye, and on his own authority also merged Shitou's troops and encamped them at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi made Wang Xu General Who Assists the State and Interior Minister of Langye, and on his own authority merged the Shitou garrison and encamped the troops at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 緒猶領其從事中郎，居中用事，寵幸當政。

translations.literal: Xu still held his Attendant-in-Ordinary post, managed affairs from the center, and by favor held power.
translations.idiomatic: Xu still held his Attendant-in-Ordinary post, managed affairs from the center, and ruled through favor.

sentences.zh: 德宗兗州刺史王恭惡國寶、王緒之亂政也，乃要荊州刺史殷仲堪剋期同舉。

translations.literal: Dezong's Inspector of Yanzhou Wang Gong hated Guobao and Xu's disorder in government; he then invited Inspector of Jingzhou Yin Zhongkan to set a date and rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong's Inspector of Yanzhou Wang Gong hated the disorder wrought by Guobao and Xu. He invited Inspector of Jingzhou Yin Zhongkan to rise on a fixed date.

sentences.zh: 王恭表德宗曰：「國寶身負莫大之罪，謹陳其狀。

translations.literal: Wang Gong memorialized Dezong: 'Guobao personally bears a crime of utmost magnitude; I respectfully set forth the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong memorialized Dezong: "Guobao bears a crime of the utmost magnitude. I respectfully set forth the facts.

sentences.zh: 前荊州刺史王悅，國寶同產弟也。

translations.literal: Former Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Yue was Guobao's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Former Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Yue was Guobao's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 受任西藩，不幸致喪。

translations.literal: He received appointment in the western frontier and unfortunately met death.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed to the western frontier, he met an untimely death.

sentences.zh: 國寶求假奔彼，遂不即路，慮臺糾察，懼於黜免，乃毀冠改服，變為婦人，與婢同載，入請相王。

translations.literal: Guobao sought leave to rush there, then did not set out on the road; fearing the court's investigation and afraid of dismissal, he destroyed his cap and changed his garments, transformed into a woman, rode in the same carriage with a maid, and entered to request audience of the Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao sought leave to rush there but never set out, fearing court investigation and dismissal. He destroyed his cap, changed into women's dress, rode with a maid in the same carriage, and entered to request audience of the Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 又先帝暴崩，莫不驚號，而國寶靦然，了無哀容，方犯閤叩扉，求行姦計，欲詐為遺詔，矯弄神器。

translations.literal: Again, when the former emperor died suddenly, none did not cry out in shock, yet Guobao was calm and composed, entirely without mourning countenance; just then he violated the gate and knocked on doors, seeking to carry out treacherous plots, wishing to forge a deathbed edict and tamper with the sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: When the former emperor died suddenly, all were shocked, yet Guobao was calm and showed no grief. He forced his way in, scheming treachery, wishing to forge a deathbed edict and seize the imperial regalia.

sentences.zh: 彰暴于外，莫不聞知。

translations.literal: His crimes were exposed outside; none did not hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: His crimes were exposed for all to hear.

sentences.zh: 讒疾二昆，過於讎敵；

translations.literal: He slandered and hated his two elder brothers, exceeding hatred of enemies;
translations.idiomatic: He slandered his two elder brothers with hatred exceeding that of enemies;

sentences.zh: 樹立私黨，遍於府朝。

translations.literal: he established private factions throughout the headquarters and court.
translations.idiomatic: he built private factions throughout the headquarters and court;

sentences.zh: 兵食資儲，斂為私積；

translations.literal: troops, grain, and stored goods he gathered as private hoards;
translations.idiomatic: he hoarded troops, grain, and stores as private wealth;

sentences.zh: 販官鬻爵，威恣百城。

translations.literal: he sold offices and peddled ranks, wielding power wantonly over a hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: he sold offices and peddled ranks, wielding power wantonly over a hundred cities;

sentences.zh: 收聚不逞，招集亡命。

translations.literal: He gathered the unbridled and recruited fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: he gathered the unbridled and recruited fugitives.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍王緒頑凶狂狡，人理不齒，同惡相成，共竊名器。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State Wang Xu was stubborn, fierce, mad, and cunning, not counted among human order; together in evil they completed each other and jointly usurped titles and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the State Wang Xu was stubborn, fierce, and cunning, beneath human regard. Together in evil they usurped titles and regalia.

sentences.zh: 自知禍惡已盈，怨集人鬼，規為大逆，蕩覆天下。

translations.literal: Knowing their calamity and evil were already full, resentment gathered from men and ghosts; they plotted great rebellion to overturn the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their crimes were full, with resentment gathering from men and spirits alike, they plotted great rebellion to overturn the realm.

sentences.zh: 昔趙鞅興晉陽之甲，夷君側之惡，臣雖駑劣，敢忘斯義。」

translations.literal: Formerly Zhao Yang raised the armor of Jinyang and extinguished evil at the ruler's side; though your servant is dull and inferior, how dare I forget this principle.'
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhao Yang raised the armies of Jinyang and extinguished evil at the ruler's side. Though I am dull and inferior, how dare I forget this duty."

sentences.zh: 恭表至，道子密欲討恭，以元顯為征虜將軍，內外諸軍潛加嚴備。

translations.literal: When Gong's memorial arrived, Daozi secretly wished to attack Gong; he made Yuanxian General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians and secretly added strict preparations to all armies within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong's memorial arrived, Daozi secretly planned to attack him. He made Yuanxian General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians and secretly strengthened all armies within and without.

sentences.zh: 而國寶惶懼，不知所為，乃遣數百人戍竹里，夜遇風雨，各散而歸。

translations.literal: Guobao was fearful and did not know what to do; he sent several hundred men to garrison Zhuli; at night they met wind and rain and each scattered and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao was terrified and sent several hundred men to garrison Zhuli. That night wind and rain scattered them, and they returned home.

sentences.zh: 緒勸國寶殺王珣，然後南征北伐，弗聽，反問計於珣。

translations.literal: Xu urged Guobao to kill Wang Xun, then campaign south and north; he did not listen, but instead asked Xun for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Xu urged Guobao to kill Wang Xun and then campaign south and north. Guobao refused and instead asked Xun for counsel.

sentences.zh: 既而懼懾，遂上表解職。

translations.literal: Soon he was afraid and cowed and memorialized to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, afraid and cowed, he memorialized to resign.

sentences.zh: 尋復悔懼，詐稱德宗復其本官。

translations.literal: Soon he again regretted and feared, and falsely claimed Dezong had restored his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he regretted and feared again, and falsely claimed Dezong had restored his original office.

sentences.zh: 道子既不能拒恭等之兵，亦欲因以委罪，乃收國寶付廷尉殺之，斬王緒於市，以悅恭等。

translations.literal: Daozi could neither refuse Gong's armies nor did he wish to; he also wished to shift blame thereby; he seized Guobao and handed him to the Court of Justice to be killed, beheaded Xu in the market, to please Gong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse Gong's armies and wishing to shift blame, Daozi seized Guobao and handed him to the Court of Justice for execution, beheaded Xu in the market, and thus pleased Gong and his allies.

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史王廞遭母喪居吳，恭板行吳國內史。

translations.literal: Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Yin, having suffered his mother's mourning, dwelt in Wu; Gong appointed him acting Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Yin, mourning his mother, dwelt in Wu. Gong appointed him acting Interior Minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 廞乃徵發吳興諸郡兵。

translations.literal: Yin then requisitioned and mobilized the troops of the commanderies of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then mobilized the troops of the Wuxing commanderies.

sentences.zh: 國寶既死，王恭使廞反於喪。

translations.literal: Guobao having died, Wang Gong ordered Yin to return from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After Guobao's death, Wang Gong ordered Yin to return from mourning.

sentences.zh: 廞謂因緣事際，可大得志，乃據吳郡，遣子弟率眾擊恭。

translations.literal: Yin thought that by the occasion of events he could greatly fulfill his ambition; he then held Wu Commandery, sent younger kinsmen to lead masses to attack Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin thought the occasion offered great ambition. He seized Wu Commandery and sent his kinsmen to attack Gong.

sentences.zh: 以女為真烈將軍，亦置官屬，領兵自衞。

translations.literal: He made his daughter General of True Valor, also installed officials, and led troops to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: He made his daughter General of True Valor, installed officials, and led troops in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 恭遣司馬劉牢之討平之。

translations.literal: Gong sent Major Liu Laozhi to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong sent Major Liu Laozhi to attack and pacify him.

sentences.zh: 德宗譙王尚之兄弟復說道子，以為藩伯強盛，宰相權弱，宜密樹置，以自藩衞。

translations.literal: Dezong's Prince of Qiao Shangzhi and his brothers again urged Daozi, saying that frontier lords were strong while the Chancellor's power was weak; they should secretly plant appointees as self-protection.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong's Prince of Qiao Shangzhi and his brothers urged Daozi again, saying frontier lords were strong while the chancellor was weak. He should secretly plant appointees as his own guard.

sentences.zh: 道子然之，分遣腹心，跨據形要，由是內外騷動。

translations.literal: Daozi agreed; he sent out trusted men in divisions to straddle and hold strategic points; thereby within and without were stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi agreed and sent trusted men to hold strategic points throughout the realm. The court was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 王恭深慮禍難，復密要殷仲堪、西中郎將庾楷、廣州刺史桓玄同會建業。

translations.literal: Wang Gong deeply feared disaster and again secretly invited Yin Zhongkan, Western Central Commander Yu Kai, and Inspector of Guangzhou Huan Xuan to meet at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong deeply feared disaster and again secretly invited Yin Zhongkan, Western Central Commander Yu Kai, and Inspector of Guangzhou Huan Xuan to meet at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 玄等響應。

translations.literal: Xuan and others responded.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the others responded.

sentences.zh: 恭抗表傳檄，以江州刺史王愉、司馬尚之為事端。

translations.literal: Gong submitted a defiant memorial and circulated a proclamation, making Inspector of Jiangzhou Wang Yu and Major Shangzhi the pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Gong submitted a defiant memorial and circulated a proclamation, citing Inspector of Jiangzhou Wang Yu and Major Shangzhi as the pretext.

sentences.zh: 仲堪遣龍驤將軍、南郡相楊佺期舟師五千發江陵，桓玄借兵於仲堪，亦給五千人。

translations.literal: Zhongkan sent General of Dragon Valor, Chancellor of Nan Commandery Yang Quanqi with a river army of five thousand from Jiangling; Huan Xuan borrowed troops from Zhongkan and was also given five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan sent General of Dragon Valor, Chancellor of Nan Commandery Yang Quanqi with five thousand river troops from Jiangling. Huan Xuan borrowed troops from Zhongkan and received five thousand men as well.

sentences.zh: 於是德宗戒嚴：加道子黃鉞；

translations.literal: Thereupon Dezong declared martial law: Daozi was given the yellow battle-axe;
translations.idiomatic: Dezong then declared martial law. Daozi was given the yellow battle-axe;

sentences.zh: 遣右將軍謝琰拒恭等；

translations.literal: the General of the Right Xie Yan was sent to resist Gong and others;
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Xie Yan was sent to resist Gong and the others;

sentences.zh: 元顯為征討都督，眾軍繼進；

translations.literal: Yuanxian was made punitive expedition commander-in-chief, and the armies followed in succession;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was made punitive expedition commander, and the armies advanced in succession;

sentences.zh: 前軍王珣領中軍府眾次于北郊；

translations.literal: Vanguard Wang Xun led the masses of the Central Army headquarters and encamped at the northern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Wang Xun led the Central Army headquarters troops and encamped at the northern suburb;

sentences.zh: 以尚之為豫州刺史，率弟恢之、允之西討楷等。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was made Inspector of Yuzhou and led his younger brothers Huizhi and Yunzhi west to campaign against Kai and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was made Inspector of Yuzhou and led his younger brothers Huizhi and Yunzhi west against Kai and the others.

sentences.zh: 皆執白虎幡居前。

translations.literal: All bore white tiger banners and went before.
translations.idiomatic: All bore white tiger banners at the fore.

sentences.zh: 王恭遣劉牢之為前鋒，次于竹里。

translations.literal: Wang Gong sent Liu Laozhi as vanguard, encamped at Zhuli.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong sent Liu Laozhi as vanguard to encamp at Zhuli.

sentences.zh: 初，道子之謀恭也，啗牢之以重賞，牢之斬恭別帥顏延、延弟強，送二級於謝琰。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Daozi's plot against Gong, he tempted Laozhi with heavy rewards; Laozhi beheaded Gong's detached commander Yan Yan and Yan's younger brother Qiang and sent the two heads to Xie Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Daozi's plot against Gong, he tempted Laozhi with heavy rewards. Laozhi beheaded Gong's detached commander Yan Yan and Yan's younger brother Qiang and sent their heads to Xie Yan.

sentences.zh: 琰與牢之俱進襲恭，恭奔于曲阿，為湖浦尉所執，送建業。

translations.literal: Yan and Laozhi together advanced to strike Gong; Gong fled to Qu'a, was seized by the Lake Ford Commandant, and sent to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Laozhi advanced together against Gong. Gong fled to Qu'a, was seized by the Lake Ford Commandant, and sent to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 尚之與庾楷子鴻戰于牛渚，斬鴻前鋒將殷萬，鴻遁還歷陽。

translations.literal: Shangzhi fought Yu Kai's son Hong at Niuzhu, beheaded Hong's vanguard general Yin Wan, and Hong fled back to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi fought Yu Kai's son Hong at Niuzhu, beheaded Hong's vanguard general Yin Wan, and Hong fled back to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 尚之猶不敢濟。

translations.literal: Shangzhi still did not dare cross.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi still did not dare cross the river.

sentences.zh: 桓玄、佺期奄至橫江，尚之等退，恢之所領外軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan and Quanqi suddenly reached Hengjiang; Shangzhi and others withdrew; the outer armies led by Huizhi were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan and Quanqi suddenly reached Hengjiang. Shangzhi and the others withdrew, and Huizhi's outer armies were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 玄等徑造石頭，仲堪繼在蕪湖，建業震駭。

translations.literal: Xuan and others went straight to Shitou; Zhongkan followed at Wuhu; Jianye was shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the others went straight to Shitou while Zhongkan followed at Wuhu. Jianye was shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 道子殺恭於倪塘。

translations.literal: Daozi killed Gong at Nitang.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi killed Gong at Nitang.

sentences.zh: 桓玄等於是走還尋陽。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan and others then fled back to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan and the others then fled back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，德宗遣使朝貢，并乞師請討姚興。

translations.literal: That winter Dezong sent envoys with tribute and also begged for troops to request campaigning against Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Dezong sent envoys with tribute and also requested troops to campaign against Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，德宗又遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, summer, Dezong again sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year, Dezong again sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 以元顯為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was made Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was made Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 道子有疾，元顯懼己弗得襲位，故矯以自授，而道子弗知。

translations.literal: Daozi fell ill; Yuanxian feared he himself could not inherit the post, and therefore forged the appointment to himself, while Daozi did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Daozi fell ill, Yuanxian feared he could not inherit the post and forged his own appointment without Daozi's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 既瘳，乃大怒，以元顯已拜，故弗復改，於是內外政事一決元顯。

translations.literal: When he recovered he was greatly angry; because Yuanxian had already received appointment, he did not change it; thereupon all affairs within and without were decided solely by Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered he was furious, but because Yuanxian had already been appointed he did not change it. Thereafter all affairs were decided solely by Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 道子少而耽酒，治日甚希，至是無事，俾晝作夜。

translations.literal: Daozi from youth was addicted to wine; days of governing grew ever rarer; at this point with nothing to do, he made day into night.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi had been addicted to wine from youth and governed ever less. Now with nothing to do, he turned day into night.

sentences.zh: 時謂道子為東錄，元顯為西錄，西府千兩輻湊，東第門設雀羅矣。

translations.literal: At the time they called Daozi the Eastern Office and Yuanxian the Western Office; the western headquarters had a thousand carts converging, while at the eastern residence gate they set a net for birds.
translations.idiomatic: People called Daozi the Eastern Office and Yuanxian the Western Office. A thousand carts converged on the western headquarters, while birds could be netted at the deserted eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 元顯年少，頓居權重，驕奢淫暴，於是遠近譏之。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was young and suddenly held heavy power; proud, extravagant, dissolute, and violent—thereupon near and far mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was young and suddenly held great power. Proud, extravagant, dissolute, and violent, he was mocked throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗新安太守孫泰以左道惑眾被戮，其兄子恩竄于海嶼，妖黨從之，至是轉眾，攻上虞，殺縣令，眾百許人徑向山陰。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dezong's Administrator of Xin'an Sun Tai was executed for using heterodox ways to delude the masses; his elder brother's son En fled to sea isles; demonic partisans followed him; by now his masses grew; he attacked Shangyu, killed the magistrate, and a band of about a hundred went straight toward Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dezong's Administrator of Xin'an Sun Tai was executed for deluding the masses with heterodox teachings. His nephew En fled to the sea isles, and demonic partisans followed him. By now his following had grown. He attacked Shangyu, killed the magistrate, and a band of about a hundred marched straight toward Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史王凝之事五斗米道，恩之來也，弗先遣軍，乃稽顙于道室，跪而呪說，指麾空中，若有處分者。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Kuaiji Wang Ningzhi practiced the Five-Pecks-of-Rice Way; when En came, he did not first send troops but kowtowed in the Way chamber, knelt and chanted spells, and directed the air as if disposing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Minister of Kuaiji Wang Ningzhi practiced the Five-Pecks-of-Rice Way. When En came, he did not send troops first but kowtowed in the Way chamber, knelt and chanted spells, and gestured in the air as if commanding an army.

sentences.zh: 官屬勸其討恩，凝之曰：「我已請大道出兵，凡諸津要各有數萬人矣。」

translations.literal: His officials urged him to attack En; Ningzhi said: 'I have already requested the Great Way to send troops—at every ford and pass there are already tens of thousands.'
translations.idiomatic: His officials urged him to attack En. Ningzhi said, "I have already requested the Great Way to send troops. At every ford and pass there are already tens of thousands."

sentences.zh: 恩漸近，乃聽遣軍。

translations.literal: As En drew near, he then allowed troops to be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Only when En drew near did he allow troops to be sent.

sentences.zh: 比兵出，恩已至矣。

translations.literal: By the time troops went out, En had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the troops went out, En had already arrived.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，凝之奔走，再宿執之。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, Ningzhi fled; after two nights he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, Ningzhi fled and was seized after two nights.

sentences.zh: 旬日，恩眾數萬，自號平東將軍，逼人士為官屬。

translations.literal: Within ten days En's masses numbered tens of thousands; he styled himself General Who Pacifies the East and compelled gentlemen to serve as officials.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days En's following numbered tens of thousands. He styled himself General Who Pacifies the East and compelled gentlemen to serve as his officials.

sentences.zh: 於是諸郡妖惑，並殺守令而應之，眾皆雲集。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commanderies were deluded by demons; all killed their administrators and magistrates and responded; the masses gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies throughout the region were deluded. They killed their administrators and magistrates and joined him, and the masses gathered like clouds.

sentences.zh: 吳國內史桓謙出奔，吳興太守謝邈被害。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Wu Huan Qian fled; Administrator of Wuxing Xie Miao was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Minister of Wu Huan Qian fled. Administrator of Wuxing Xie Miao was killed.

sentences.zh: 自德宗以來，內外乖貳，石頭以外，皆專之於荊、江，自江以西則受命於豫州，京口暨于江北皆兗州刺史劉牢之等所制，德宗政令所行，唯三吳而已。

translations.literal: Since Dezong, within and without were divided in two; outside Shitou all was monopolized by Jing and Jiang; west of the river orders came from Yuzhou; Jingkou and north of the river were all controlled by Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Laozhi and others; Dezong's government orders were enforced only in the Three Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Since Dezong's reign, court and provinces had fallen apart. Beyond Shitou, Jing and Jiang monopolized power; west of the river, Yuzhou held sway; Jingkou and the lands north of the river were controlled by Inspector of Yanzhou Liu Laozhi and others. Dezong's orders reached only the Three Wu.

sentences.zh: 恩既作亂，八郡盡為賊場，及丹陽諸縣處處蜂起，建業轉成蹙弱。

translations.literal: En having rebelled, eight commanderies all became bandit territory; in Danyang the various counties rose like bees everywhere; Jianye turned ever more cramped and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Once En rebelled, eight commanderies became bandit territory, counties throughout Danyang rose everywhere, and Jianye grew ever more desperate.

sentences.zh: 且妖惑之徒，多潛都邑，人情危懼，恒慮大兵竊發。

translations.literal: Moreover the demon-deluded masses mostly lurked in the capital; human sentiment was fearful; they constantly feared great armies would rise in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Demon-deluded followers lurked in the capital. The people lived in fear, constantly dreading a sudden uprising.

sentences.zh: 於是眾軍戒嚴，劉牢之共衞將軍謝琰討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the armies declared martial law; Liu Laozhi and Co-Guardian General Xie Yan campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: The armies declared martial law. Liu Laozhi and Co-Guardian General Xie Yan campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 賊等禁令不行，肆意殺戮，士庶死者不可勝計，或醢諸縣令以食其妻子，不肯者輒支解之，其虐如此。

translations.literal: The bandits' prohibitions were not enforced; they killed at will; gentlemen and commoners who died could not be counted; some pickled magistrates of various counties to feed their wives and children; those who refused were at once dismembered—such was their cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels enforced no discipline and killed at will. The dead among gentry and commoners were beyond counting. Some pickled magistrates to feed their wives and children; those who refused were dismembered. Such was their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 驃騎長史王平之死未葬，恩剖棺焚屍，以其頭為穢器。

translations.literal: Agile Cavalry Chief Clerk Wang Pingzhi had died and was not yet buried; En opened the coffin, burned the corpse, and used his head as a filthy vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Agile Cavalry Chief Clerk Wang Pingzhi had died and was not yet buried. En opened the coffin, burned the corpse, and used his head as a filthy vessel.

sentences.zh: 牢之率軍討破之。

translations.literal: Laozhi led the army to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi led the army and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 琰將至吳興，賊徒遁走，驅逼士庶，奔于山陰。

translations.literal: Yan was about to reach Wuxing; the bandit masses fled, driving gentlemen and commoners, who ran to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: As Yan was about to reach Wuxing, the rebels fled, driving gentry and commoners before them toward Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 諸妖亂之家，婦女尤甚，未得去者，皆盛飾嬰兒投之于水而告之曰：「賀汝先登仙堂，我尋復就汝也。」

translations.literal: Among households of the various demonic disorders, women especially; those who could not leave all lavishly adorned their infants and cast them into the water, telling them: 'Congratulations—you ascend the immortal hall first; I shall soon follow you.'
translations.idiomatic: Among the households caught in the demonic turmoil, women suffered most. Those who could not flee lavishly adorned their infants and cast them into the water, saying, "Congratulations—you ascend the immortal hall first. I shall soon follow you."

sentences.zh: 賊既走散，邑屋焚毀，郛郭之中，時見人跡，經月乃漸有歸者。

translations.literal: The bandits having scattered, towns and houses were burned; within the outer walls human traces were sometimes seen; after a month there were gradually those who returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels scattered, towns and houses lay burned. Human traces appeared within the outer walls only after a month, when people gradually began to return.

sentences.zh: 謝琰留屯烏程，遣其將高素助牢之。

translations.literal: Xie Yan remained encamped at Wucheng and sent his general Gao Su to assist Laozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan remained encamped at Wucheng and sent his general Gao Su to assist Laozhi.

sentences.zh: 牢之率眾軍濟江。

translations.literal: Laozhi led the mass of armies across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi led the armies across the river.

sentences.zh: 初，孫恩聞八郡響應也，告諸官屬曰：「天下無復事矣，當與諸君朝服而至建業。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sun En heard eight commanderies had responded, he told his officials: 'Under Heaven there are no more affairs—we shall with you all come to Jianye in court dress.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sun En heard that eight commanderies had responded, he told his officials, "Under Heaven there is nothing left to do—we shall come to Jianye in court dress."

sentences.zh: 既聞牢之臨江，復曰：「我割據浙江，不失作勾踐也。」

translations.literal: When he heard Laozhi was approaching the river, he again said: 'If I hold Zhejiang, it is no loss to be Goujian.'
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Laozhi was approaching the river, he said, "If I hold Zhejiang, I can still be Goujian."

sentences.zh: 尋知牢之已濟，乃曰：「孤不耻走。」

translations.literal: Soon learning Laozhi had crossed, he then said: 'I am not ashamed to flee.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon learning Laozhi had crossed, he said, "I am not ashamed to flee."

sentences.zh: 於是乃走。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fled.
translations.idiomatic: And he fled.

sentences.zh: 緣道多遺珍寶，牢之將士爭取之，不得窮追。

translations.literal: Along the road he left many precious things; Laozhi's officers and soldiers scrambled to take them and could not pursue to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Along the road he dropped many treasures. Laozhi's soldiers scrambled for them and could not pursue to the end.

sentences.zh: 恩復入於海。

translations.literal: En again entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: En again fled to the sea.

sentences.zh: 初，三吳困於虐亂，皆企望牢之、高素等。

translations.literal: Earlier the Three Wu, afflicted by savage disorder, all looked in hope to Laozhi, Gao Su, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Three Wu, afflicted by savage disorder, had all looked to Laozhi, Gao Su, and the others in hope.

sentences.zh: 既至，放肆抄暴，百姓咸怨毒失望焉。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they indulged in plunder and violence; the common people all resented them bitterly and lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, they plundered without restraint. The people resented them bitterly and lost all hope.

sentences.zh: 孫恩在海，妖眾轉復從之。

translations.literal: Sun En was at sea; demonic masses again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En was at sea, and demonic followers again gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 既破永嘉、臨海，復入山陰。

translations.literal: Having defeated Yongjia and Linhai, he again entered Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Having overrun Yongjia and Linhai, he again entered Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 謝琰戰歿。

translations.literal: Xie Yan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan died in battle.

sentences.zh: 於是建業大震，遣冠軍將軍、東海太守桓不才，輔國將軍孫無終，廣陵相高雅之等東討恩。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jianye was greatly shaken; they sent Champion General, Administrator of Donghai Huan Bucai, General Who Assists the State Sun Wuzhong, Chancellor of Guangling Gao Yazhi, and others east to campaign against En.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye was shaken. They sent Champion General, Administrator of Donghai Huan Bucai, General Who Assists the State Sun Wuzhong, Chancellor of Guangling Gao Yazhi, and others east against En.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守庾恒慮妖黨復發，大行誅戮，殺男女數千人。

translations.literal: Administrator of Wuxing Yu Heng feared the demonic faction would rise again and carried out great executions, killing several thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Wuxing Yu Heng feared the demonic faction would rise again and carried out mass executions, killing several thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 孫恩復破高雅之於餘姚，雅之走還山陰。

translations.literal: Sun En again defeated Gao Yazhi at Yuyao; Yazhi fled back to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En again defeated Gao Yazhi at Yuyao, and Yazhi fled back to Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 元顯自為後將軍、開府儀同三司、都督十六州，本官悉如故；

translations.literal: Yuanxian made himself Rear General, Equal in Three Offices with an opened headquarters, and Commander-in-Chief of sixteen provinces; his original offices all remained as before;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian made himself Rear General, Equal in Three Offices with an opened headquarters, and Commander-in-Chief of sixteen provinces, while retaining his original offices;

sentences.zh: 封子彥章為東海王，食吳興四萬餘戶，清選文學臣僚，吏兵一同宗國。

translations.literal: he enfeoffed his son Yanzhang as King of Donghai with a fief of more than forty thousand households in Wuxing, carefully selected literary officials, and made clerks and soldiers the same as a royal state.
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed his son Yanzhang as King of Donghai with a fief of more than forty thousand households in Wuxing, selected literary officials, and gave him clerks and soldiers like a royal state.

sentences.zh: 孫恩浮海奄至京口，戰士十萬，劉牢之隔在山陰，眾軍懼不敢旋，恩遂徑向建業。

translations.literal: Sun En crossed the sea and suddenly reached Jingkou with a hundred thousand warriors; Liu Laozhi was blocked at Shanyin; the armies feared and dared not turn back; En then went straight toward Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En crossed the sea and suddenly reached Jingkou with a hundred thousand warriors. Liu Laozhi was blocked at Shanyin, the armies feared to turn back, and En marched straight on Jianye.

sentences.zh: 德宗惶駭，遽召豫州刺史司馬尚之。

translations.literal: Dezong was terrified and hastily summoned Inspector of Yuzhou Sima Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was terrified and hastily summoned Inspector of Yuzhou Sima Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 于時中外驚擾，而元顯置酒高會，道子唯日祈于鍾山。

translations.literal: At that time within and without were alarmed and disturbed, yet Yuanxian set out wine in high feast; Daozi only prayed daily at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in alarm, yet Yuanxian held high feasts while Daozi prayed daily at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 恩來漸近，百姓忷懼。

translations.literal: As En drew nearer, the common people were fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: As En drew nearer, the people were seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 尚之率精銳馳至，徑屯積弩堂。

translations.literal: Shangzhi led elite troops galloping to arrive and encamped directly at the Accumulated Crossbows Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi led elite troops to the city and encamped at the Accumulated Crossbows Hall.

sentences.zh: 恩時泝風，不得疾行，數日乃至白石。

translations.literal: En at the time faced contrary wind and could not travel swiftly; several days passed before he reached Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: En faced a contrary wind and could not travel swiftly. Several days passed before he reached Baishi.

sentences.zh: 恩本以諸軍分散，欲掩不備，知尚之尚在建業，復聞牢之不還，不敢上，乃走向郁洲。

translations.literal: En had thought the armies were scattered and wished to strike unprepared; learning Shangzhi was still at Jianye and again hearing Laozhi would not return, he dared not advance and went toward Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: En had thought the armies were scattered and wished to strike unprepared. Learning Shangzhi was still at Jianye and that Laozhi would not return, he dared not advance and turned toward Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 恩別帥盧循攻沒廣陵，虜掠而去。

translations.literal: En's detached commander Lu Xun attacked and overran Guangling, plundered, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: En's detached commander Lu Xun overran Guangling, plundered it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 桓玄聞孫恩之逼也，乃建牙戒嚴，表求征討。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan heard of Sun En's pressing threat, raised his command banner and declared martial law, and memorialized requesting a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan heard of Sun En's threat, he raised his command banner, declared martial law, and memorialized requesting a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 時恩去未遠，玄表復至，元顯等大懼，急遣止玄。

translations.literal: En had not gone far; Xuan's memorial arrived again; Yuanxian and others were greatly afraid and urgently sent orders to stop Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: En had not gone far when Xuan's memorial arrived again. Yuanxian and the others were terrified and urgently ordered him to stop.

sentences.zh: 庾楷密使自結於元顯，說玄大失人情，眾不為用，若朝廷遣軍，己當內應。

translations.literal: Yu Kai secretly sent envoys to ally with Yuanxian, saying Xuan had greatly lost human sentiment and the masses would not serve him; if the court sent troops, he himself would respond from within.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai secretly allied with Yuanxian, saying Xuan had lost all popular support and that if the court sent troops, he would respond from within.

sentences.zh: 元顯得書大喜，遣張法順謀于劉牢之，牢之同許焉。

translations.literal: Yuanxian received the letter and was greatly pleased; he sent Zhang Fashun to plot with Liu Laozhi; Laozhi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was delighted by the letter and sent Zhang Fashun to plot with Liu Laozhi, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是徵兵裝艦，將謀西討。

translations.literal: Thereupon they mobilized troops and fitted out ships, planning a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: They mobilized troops, fitted out ships, and planned a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 德宗改年曰元興，以元顯為大都督討玄。

translations.literal: Dezong changed the era to Yuanxing and made Yuanxian Grand Commander-in-Chief to attack Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong changed the era to Yuanxing and made Yuanxian Grand Commander-in-Chief to attack Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄軍至，元顯不戰而敗，父子並為玄所殺。

translations.literal: Xuan's army arrived; Yuanxian was defeated without fighting; father and son were both killed by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan's army arrived, Yuanxian was defeated without a fight. Father and son were both killed by Xuan.

sentences.zh: 後改年為大亨。

translations.literal: Later the era was changed to Daheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later the era was changed to Daheng.

sentences.zh: 天興六年十月，德宗遣使朝京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Tianxing, Dezong sent envoys to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Tianxing, Dezong sent envoys to court at the Northern Wei capital.

sentences.zh: 時盧循執德宗廣州刺史吳隱之，自號平南將軍、廣州刺史，令其黨徐道覆據始興，餘郡皆以親黨居之。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Xun held Dezong's Inspector of Guangzhou Wu Yinshi, styled himself General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guangzhou, ordered his partisan Xu Daofu to hold Shixing, and placed kinsmen and partisans in the remaining commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun held Dezong's Inspector of Guangzhou Wu Yinshi, styled himself General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guangzhou, placed his partisan Xu Daofu at Shixing, and installed kinsmen in the remaining commanderies.

sentences.zh: 德宗復僭立於江陵，改年義熙。

translations.literal: Dezong again usurped the throne at Jiangling and changed the era to Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong again usurped the throne at Jiangling and changed the era to Yixi.

sentences.zh: 尚書陶夔迎德宗，達于板橋，大風暴起，龍舟沉沒，死者十餘人。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Tao Kui welcomed Dezong and reached Banqiao; a great windstorm arose; the dragon boat sank; more than ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Tao Kui welcomed Dezong to Banqiao. A great storm arose, the dragon boat sank, and more than ten men died.

sentences.zh: 德宗發江陵至尋陽，其益州刺史毛璩、參軍譙縱反，攻涪城，克之，遂以益州叛德宗。

translations.literal: Dezong set out from Jiangling to Xunyang; his Inspector of Yizhou Mao Qu and Adjutant Qiao Zong rebelled, attacked Fucheng, took it, and then with Yizhou rebelled against Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong set out from Jiangling to Xunyang. His Inspector of Yizhou Mao Qu and Adjutant Qiao Zong rebelled, took Fucheng, and rebelled with Yizhou against Dezong.

sentences.zh: 德宗發姑熟，還建業。

translations.literal: Dezong set out from Guniu and returned to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong set out from Guniu and returned to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 六月，太祖遣軍攻德宗鉅鹿太守賀申，申舉城降。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Founder Emperor sent troops to attack Dezong's Administrator of Julu He Shen; Shen raised the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Founder Emperor sent troops against Dezong's Administrator of Julu He Shen, who surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 永興二年，盧循復起於嶺南，殺德宗江州刺史何無忌於石城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxing, Lu Xun again rose in Lingnan and killed Dezong's Inspector of Jiangzhou He Wuji at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxing, Lu Xun again rose in Lingnan and killed Dezong's Inspector of Jiangzhou He Wuji at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 咸欲以德宗北走，知循未下乃止。

translations.literal: All wished Dezong to flee north; learning Xun had not yet been subdued, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: All wished Dezong to flee north, but when they learned Xun had not yet been subdued, they stopped.

sentences.zh: 裕令撫軍劉毅討循，敗於桑落洲，步走而還。

translations.literal: Yu ordered Pacification General Liu Yi to campaign against Xun; he was defeated at Sangluo Isle, went on foot, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu ordered Pacification General Liu Yi against Xun. Yi was defeated at Sangluo Isle and returned on foot.

sentences.zh: 裕黨孟昶、諸葛長民等勸裕擁德宗過江，裕不從。

translations.literal: Yu's partisans Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others urged Yu to escort Dezong across the river; Yu did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's partisans Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others urged him to escort Dezong across the river, but Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 神瑞二年，德宗遣廣武將軍玄文、石齊朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenrui, Dezong sent General of Broad Martial Might Xuan Wen and Shi Qi with tribute to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenrui, Dezong sent General of Broad Martial Might Xuan Wen and Shi Qi with tribute to court.

sentences.zh: [9]泰常初，劉裕征姚泓。

translations.literal: [9] At the beginning of Taichang, Liu Yu campaigned against Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: [9] At the beginning of Taichang, Liu Yu campaigned against Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: [10]二年，太宗遣長孫道生、娥清破其將朱超石於石河，[11]擒騎將楊豐，斬首千七百餘級。

translations.literal: [10] In the second year, Emperor Taizong sent Zhangsun Daosheng and E Qing to defeat his general Zhu Chaoshi at Shihe; [11] they captured Cavalry General Yang Feng and beheaded more than seventeen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: [10] In the second year, Emperor Taizong sent Zhangsun Daosheng and E Qing to defeat his general Zhu Chaoshi at Shihe. [11] They captured Cavalry General Yang Feng and took more than seventeen hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 三年，德宗死，弟德文僭立。

translations.literal: In the third year Dezong died; his younger brother Dewen usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Dezong died and his younger brother Dewen usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 四年，改年曰元熙五年，德文禪位於裕，裕封德文為零陵王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the era was changed to the fifth year of Yuanxi; Dewen abdicated to Yu; Yu enfeoffed Dewen as King of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the era was changed to the fifth year of Yuanxi. Dewen abdicated to Liu Yu, who enfeoffed him as King of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 德文后河南褚氏，兄季之、弟淡之雖德文姻戚，而盡心於裕。

translations.literal: Dewen's consort was Lady Chu of Henan; her elder brother Jizhi and younger brother Danzhi, though Dewen's kin by marriage, devoted themselves wholly to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen's consort was Lady Chu of Henan. Her elder brother Jizhi and younger brother Danzhi, though Dewen's kin by marriage, devoted themselves wholly to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 德文每生男，輒令方便殺焉。

translations.literal: Whenever Dewen bore a son, they at once found means to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Dewen bore a son, they found means to kill him.

sentences.zh: 或誘內人，密加毒害，前後非一。

translations.literal: Sometimes they enticed inner attendants to secretly add poison—more than once before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they enticed inner attendants to poison the infants secretly—more than once.

sentences.zh: 及德文被廢，囚於秣陵宮，常懼見禍，與褚氏共止一室，慮有鴆毒，自煮食於前。

translations.literal: When Dewen was deposed and imprisoned in the Moling Palace, he constantly feared disaster; he and Lady Chu shared one room; fearing poisoned wine, he cooked his own food before him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dewen was deposed and imprisoned in the Moling Palace, he lived in constant fear. He and Lady Chu shared one room, and fearing poisoned food, he cooked for himself.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉裕將殺之，不欲遣人入內，令淡之兄弟視褚氏，褚氏出別宮，於是兵乃踰垣而入，進藥於德文。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liu Yu was about to kill him and did not wish to send men inside; he ordered Danzhi and his brothers to visit Lady Chu; Lady Chu went out to a separate palace; then soldiers crossed the wall and entered and presented medicine to Dewen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Liu Yu planned to kill him and did not wish to send men inside. He ordered Danzhi and his brothers to visit Lady Chu, who was taken to a separate palace. Soldiers then scaled the wall, entered, and presented poison to Dewen.

sentences.zh: 德文不肯飲，曰：「佛教，自殺者不復人身。」

translations.literal: Dewen refused to drink and said: 'In Buddhism, one who kills himself does not regain human form.'
translations.idiomatic: Dewen refused to drink, saying, "In Buddhism, one who kills himself does not regain human form."

sentences.zh: 乃以被掩殺之。

translations.literal: They then smothered him with a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: They smothered him with a quilt instead.

sentences.zh: 自叡之僭江南，至於德文之死，君弱臣強，不相羈制，賞罰號令，皆出權寵，危亡廢奪，釁故相尋，所謂夷狄之有君，不若諸夏之亡也。

translations.literal: From Rui's usurpation south of the Yangtze to Dewen's death, the lord was weak and ministers strong, not restraining each other; rewards, punishments, and orders all came from favored power; peril, ruin, deposition, and seizure followed one after another in provocations—the so-called 'barbarians have a lord, yet it is not like the Central States without one.'
translations.idiomatic: From Rui's usurpation south of the Yangtze to Dewen's death, the ruler was weak and ministers strong, unrestrained by one another. Rewards, punishments, and orders all issued from favored power. Peril, ruin, deposition, and usurpation followed in endless succession—the proverb says barbarians may have a lord, yet it is not like the Central States without one.

sentences.zh: 賨李雄，字仲儁，蓋廩君之苗裔也。

translations.literal: Cong Li Xiong, styled Zhongjun, was probably a descendant of Lord Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Cong Li Xiong, styled Zhongjun, was probably a descendant of Lord Lin.

sentences.zh: 其先居於巴西宕渠。

translations.literal: His ancestors dwelt in Dangqu in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors dwelt in Dangqu in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 秦并天下，為黔中郡，薄賦其民，口出錢三十，[12]巴人謂賦為「賨」，因為名焉。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm it became Qianzhong Commandery, with light taxation on its people, thirty cash per mouth; [12] the Ba people called tax 'cong,' and from this came the name.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the realm the region became Qianzhong Commandery, with light taxation of thirty cash per person. [12] The Ba people called tax "cong," and from this came the name.

sentences.zh: 後徙櫟陽。

translations.literal: Later they moved to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later they moved to Liyang.

sentences.zh: [13]祖慕，魏東羌獵將。

translations.literal: [13] His grandfather Mu was a hunting general of the Eastern Qiang in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: [13] His grandfather Mu was a hunting general of the Eastern Qiang in Wei.

sentences.zh: 慕有五子，輔、特、庠、流、驤。

translations.literal: Mu had five sons: Fu, Te, Xiang, Liu, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Mu had five sons: Fu, Te, Xiang, Liu, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 晉惠時，關西擾亂，頻歲大飢，特兄弟率流民數萬家就穀漢中，遂入巴蜀。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Hui of Jin, Guanxi was disturbed, and for successive years there was great famine; the Te brothers led tens of thousands of refugee households seeking grain to Hanzhong, then entered Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Hui of Jin, Guanxi was in turmoil and famine struck year after year. The Te brothers led tens of thousands of refugee households seeking grain to Hanzhong, then entered Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 時晉益州刺史趙廞反叛，特兄弟起兵誅之，晉拜特宣威將軍、長樂鄉侯，流奮威將軍、武陽侯。

translations.literal: At the time Jin's Inspector of Yizhou Zhao Xin rebelled; the Te brothers raised troops to execute him; Jin appointed Te General Who Proclaims Might and Marquis of Changle Township, and Liu General Who Exerts Might and Marquis of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Inspector of Yizhou Zhao Xin rebelled. The Te brothers raised troops to execute him. Jin appointed Te General Who Proclaims Might and Marquis of Changle Township, and Liu General Who Exerts Might and Marquis of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 流民閻式等推特行鎮北大將軍，承制封拜，流行鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Refugee Yan Shi and others urged Te to act as General Who Pacifies the North, and by imperial commission enfeoffed and appointed; Liu acted as General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Refugee leader Yan Shi and others urged Te to act as General Who Pacifies the North with commission to enfeoff and appoint officials. Liu acted as General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 後與晉益州刺史羅尚相攻。

translations.literal: Later they fought with Jin's Inspector of Yizhou Luo Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Later they fought Jin's Inspector of Yizhou Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 昭帝七年，特自稱大將軍、大都督，號年建初。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Emperor Zhao, Te styled himself Grand General and Grand Commander-in-Chief and styled the era Jianchu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Emperor Zhao, Te styled himself Grand General and Grand Commander-in-Chief and named the era Jianchu.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，為尚所殺，流代統兵事。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, he was killed by Shang; Liu succeeded in command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, he was killed by Shang. Liu succeeded to command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 流字玄通，自稱大都督、大將軍。

translations.literal: Liu, styled Xuantong, styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, styled Xuantong, styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 流病將死，以後事屬雄，雄，特少子也。

translations.literal: Liu, ill and about to die, entrusted later affairs to Xiong; Xiong was Te's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu lay dying, he entrusted affairs to Xiong, Te's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 雄自稱大都督、大將軍。

translations.literal: Xiong styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 十年，僭稱成都王，號年建興，置百官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he usurped the title King of Chengdu, styled the era Jianxing, and installed the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he usurped the title King of Chengdu, styled the era Jianxing, and installed the full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 時涪陵人范長生頗有術數，雄篤信之，勸雄即真。

translations.literal: At the time Fuling man Fan Changsheng was skilled in occult arts; Xiong deeply trusted him and urged Xiong to take the true throne.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling man Fan Changsheng was skilled in occult arts. Xiong deeply trusted him and urged him to take the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 十二年，僭稱皇帝，號大成，改年為晏平，拜長生為天地太師，領丞相，西山王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he usurped the title Emperor, styled the state Dacheng, changed the era to Yanping, and appointed Changsheng Grand Master of Heaven and Earth, Chancellor, and King of Xishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he usurped the imperial title, named his state Dacheng, changed the era to Yanping, and appointed Changsheng Grand Master of Heaven and Earth, Chancellor, and King of Xishan.

sentences.zh: 又改年為玉衡。

translations.literal: He again changed the era to Yuheng.
translations.idiomatic: He again changed the era to Yuheng.

sentences.zh: 雄以中原喪亂，乃頻遣使朝貢，與穆帝請分天下。

translations.literal: Xiong, because the Central Plain was in disorder, then frequently sent envoys with tribute and asked Emperor Mu to divide the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Central Plain was in disorder, Xiong frequently sent envoys with tribute and asked Emperor Mu to divide the realm.

sentences.zh: 雄捨其子，而立兄盪第四子班為太子。

translations.literal: Xiong set aside his son and installed his elder brother Dang's fourth son Ban as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong set aside his own son and installed his elder brother Dang's fourth son Ban as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 烈帝六年，雄死，班代統任。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Emperor Lie, Xiong died; Ban succeeded to rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Emperor Lie, Xiong died and Ban succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 雄子期，殺班而自立。

translations.literal: Xiong's son Qi killed Ban and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's son Qi killed Ban and installed himself.

sentences.zh: 期，字世運，雄第四子也。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Shiyun, was Xiong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, styled Shiyun, was Xiong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 改年為玉恒。

translations.literal: He changed the era to Yuheng.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era to Yuheng.

sentences.zh: 驤子壽自涪城襲克成都，廢期為卭都公，期自殺。

translations.literal: Xiang's son Shou from Fucheng raided and took Chengdu, deposed Qi as Duke of Qiongdu, and Qi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's son Shou raided from Fucheng and took Chengdu, deposed Qi as Duke of Qiongdu, and Qi killed himself.

sentences.zh: 壽，字武考。

translations.literal: Shou, styled Wukao.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, styled Wukao.

sentences.zh: 初為雄大將軍，封建寧王，以南中十二郡為建寧國，至期，徙封漢王。

translations.literal: At first he was Xiong's Grand General and enfeoffed as King of Jianning, with the twelve commanderies of Nanzhong as the state of Jianning; at Qi's time he was transferred and enfeoffed as King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was Xiong's Grand General and enfeoffed as King of Jianning, with the twelve commanderies of Nanzhong as his kingdom. Under Qi he was transferred and enfeoffed as King of Han.

sentences.zh: 既廢期自立，改年為漢興，又改號曰漢，時建國元年也。

translations.literal: Having deposed Qi and installed himself, he changed the era to Hanxing, again changed the state title to Han—it was the first year of Jianguo.
translations.idiomatic: Having deposed Qi and installed himself, he changed the era to Hanxing and the state title to Han—the first year of Jianguo.

sentences.zh: 壽廣漢太守李乾與大臣謀欲廢壽，壽懼，令子廣與大臣盟於殿前。

translations.literal: Shou's Administrator of Guanghan Li Qian plotted with great ministers to depose Shou; Shou feared this and ordered his son Guang to ally with the great ministers in oath before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's Administrator of Guanghan Li Qian plotted with ministers to depose him. Shou feared this and had his son Guang swear alliance with the ministers before the hall.

sentences.zh: 壽聞鄴中殷實，宮觀美麗，石虎以殺罰御下，控制邦域城鎮，深用欣慕。

translations.literal: Shou heard that Ye was rich and substantial, palaces and towers beautiful; Shi Hu used killing and punishment to control subordinates and command the realm's cities and towns—he deeply admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Shou heard that Ye was rich, its palaces beautiful, and that Shi Hu controlled subordinates through killing and punishment and held the realm's cities in his grip. He deeply admired this.

sentences.zh: 吏民有小過，輒殺之以立威名。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners with small faults were at once killed to establish a reputation for awe.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners with small faults were at once killed to establish his reputation for terror.

sentences.zh: 又以郊甸未實，城邑空虛，工匠器械，事用不足，乃徙民三丁已上於成都，興尚方、御府，發州郡工巧以充之。

translations.literal: Also because the suburbs were not filled and cities empty, craftsmen and tools insufficient for needs, he moved people of three males and above to Chengdu, established the Imperial Workshop and Palace Storehouse, and mobilized skilled artisans from provinces and commanderies to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the suburbs were empty, cities deserted, and craftsmen and tools insufficient, he moved households with three adult males or more to Chengdu, established the Imperial Workshop and Palace Storehouse, and mobilized skilled artisans from the provinces to fill them.

sentences.zh: [14]廣修宮室，引水入城，務於奢侈，百姓疲於使役，民多嗟怨，思亂者十室而九。

translations.literal: [14] He broadly repaired palaces, led water into the city, pursued extravagance; the common people were exhausted by corvée; many sighed in resentment; those thinking of disorder were nine in ten households.
translations.idiomatic: [14] He broadly repaired palaces, led water into the city, and pursued extravagance. The people were exhausted by corvée, sighed in resentment, and nine households in ten thought of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 其尚書左僕射蔡興直言切諫，壽以為謗訕，誅之。

translations.literal: His Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Cai Xing spoke bluntly in sharp remonstrance; Shou considered it slander and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: His Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Cai Xing remonstrated bluntly. Shou deemed it slander and executed him.

sentences.zh: 其臣龔壯作詩七首，託言應璩以諷壽。

translations.literal: His minister Gong Zhuang composed seven poems, using Ying Qu as a pretext to satirize Shou.
translations.idiomatic: His minister Gong Zhuang composed seven poems under the name of Ying Qu to satirize Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽報曰：「省詩知意。

translations.literal: Shou replied: 'I have read the poems and know the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shou replied, "I have read the poems and know your intent.

sentences.zh: 若今人所作，賢哲之話言；

translations.literal: If composed by men of today, they are the words of sages and worthies;
translations.idiomatic: If composed by men of today, they are the words of sages;

sentences.zh: 古人所作，死鬼之常辭耳。」

translations.literal: if composed by men of antiquity, they are merely the usual phrases of dead ghosts.'
translations.idiomatic: if composed by men of antiquity, they are merely the usual phrases of dead ghosts."

sentences.zh: 動慕漢武、魏明政法，耻聞父兄時事。

translations.literal: He was moved to admire the government methods of Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Ming of Wei, and was ashamed to hear of his father and elder brothers' affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He admired the government methods of Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Ming of Wei and was ashamed to hear of his father and elder brothers' affairs.

sentences.zh: 上書者不得言先世政化，自以勝之也。

translations.literal: Memorializers were not permitted to speak of former generations' government and transformation; he considered himself superior.
translations.idiomatic: Memorializers were forbidden to speak of former generations' governance, for he considered himself superior.

sentences.zh: 及壽疾病，見李期、蔡興為祟，遂死。

translations.literal: When Shou fell ill, he saw Li Qi and Cai Xing as apparitions haunting him, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou fell ill, he saw Li Qi and Cai Xing as vengeful spirits and died.

sentences.zh: 子勢統任。

translations.literal: His son Shi succeeded to rule.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 勢，字子仁。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Ziren.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Ziren.

sentences.zh: 既立，改年為太和。

translations.literal: Having been installed, he changed the era to Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed, he changed the era to Taihe.

sentences.zh: 遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 又改為嘉寧。

translations.literal: He again changed it to Jianing.
translations.idiomatic: He again changed the era to Jianing.

sentences.zh: 勢弟漢王廣以勢無子，請為太弟，勢不許。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother the King of Han Guang, because Shi had no son, requested to be Grand Heir; Shi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother the King of Han Guang, because Shi had no son, requested to be Grand Heir, but Shi refused.

sentences.zh: 廣欲襲勢，勢使其太保李弈擊廣於涪城，克之，貶為臨卭侯，廣尋自殺。

translations.literal: Guang wished to strike Shi; Shi sent his Grand Mentor Li Yi to attack Guang at Fucheng, overcame him, demoted him to Marquis of Linqiong, and Guang soon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guang plotted to strike Shi. Shi sent his Grand Mentor Li Yi against him at Fucheng, defeated him, demoted him to Marquis of Linqiong, and Guang soon killed himself.

sentences.zh: 勢既驕吝，荒於酒色，至殺人而取其妻，又納李弈女為后。

translations.literal: Shi was proud and stingy, dissolute in wine and women, even killing men and taking their wives; he also took Li Yi's daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was proud and stingy, dissolute in wine and women, even killing men and taking their wives. He also took Li Yi's daughter as empress.

sentences.zh: 耽於淫樂，不恤國事，夷獠叛亂，境土減削，累年荒儉。
