translations.literal: Indulging in licentious pleasure, he did not care for state affairs; Yi and Liao rebelled; territory shrank; for successive years there was famine and want.
translations.idiomatic: Indulging in licentious pleasure, he neglected state affairs. Yi and Liao peoples rebelled, territory shrank, and famine struck year after year.

sentences.zh: 性多忌害，誅殘大臣，刑罰酷濫。

translations.literal: His nature was full of jealousy and harm; he executed and mutilated great ministers; punishments were cruel and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous and harmful by nature, he executed great ministers and imposed cruel, excessive punishments.

sentences.zh: 斥外父祖舊臣，親任近習，左右小人因行威福。

translations.literal: He expelled his father's and grandfather's old ministers and personally trusted close attendants; petty men at his side wielded authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: He expelled his father's and grandfather's old ministers, trusted only close attendants, and petty men at his side wielded power.

sentences.zh: 修飾室宇，羣臣諫諍，一無所納。

translations.literal: He adorned palaces and chambers; when ministers remonstrated, he accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: He adorned palaces and chambers and accepted none of his ministers' remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 又常居內，少見公卿。

translations.literal: He also constantly dwelt within and rarely saw the Three Excellencies and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly dwelt within the palace and rarely saw the great ministers.

sentences.zh: 史官屢陳災譴，乃加相國董皎大都督，以名位優之，實望與分災眚。

translations.literal: Historiographers repeatedly reported calamities and warnings; he then added Chancellor Dong Jiao as Grand Commander-in-Chief, honoring him in name and rank, in truth hoping to share the calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Historiographers repeatedly reported calamities. He then made Chancellor Dong Jiao Grand Commander-in-Chief, honoring him in name while hoping to share the blame for disasters.

sentences.zh: 建國十年，司馬聃將桓溫伐之，勢降於溫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jianguo, Sima Dan led Huan Wen to campaign against him; Shi surrendered to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jianguo, Sima Dan led Huan Wen against him, and Shi surrendered to Wen.

sentences.zh: 先是頻有怪異。

translations.literal: Before this there were frequent strange occurrences.
translations.idiomatic: Before this there had been frequent strange occurrences.

sentences.zh: 成都北鄉有人望見女子避入草中，往視，見物如人，有身形頭目，無手足，能動搖，不能言。

translations.literal: In the northern village of Chengdu someone saw a woman flee into the grass; going to look, he saw a thing like a person, with body form, head, and eyes, but no hands or feet; it could sway but could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: In a northern village of Chengdu someone saw a woman flee into the grass. Going to look, he found a humanlike thing with body, head, and eyes but no hands or feet. It could sway but could not speak.

sentences.zh: 廣漢馬生角，各長寸半。

translations.literal: In Guanghan horses grew horns, each a inch and a half long.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghan horses grew horns, each an inch and a half long.

sentences.zh: 有馬駒，一頭、二身、六耳、無目、二陰，一牝一牡。

translations.literal: There was a colt with one head, two bodies, six ears, no eyes, and two genitals—one female, one male.
translations.idiomatic: A colt appeared with one head, two bodies, six ears, no eyes, and two genitals—one female, one male.

sentences.zh: 又有驢，無皮毛，飲食數日而死。

translations.literal: There was also a donkey without skin or fur; after eating and drinking for several days it died.
translations.idiomatic: A donkey appeared without skin or fur and died after eating and drinking for several days.

sentences.zh: 江南雨血，地生毛。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan it rained blood; the ground grew hair.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan it rained blood, and hair grew from the ground.

sentences.zh: 江源又生草，高七八尺，華葉皆赤，子青如牛角。

translations.literal: At the source of the river grass again grew, seven or eight feet high; flowers and leaves were all red; seeds were green like ox horns.
translations.idiomatic: At the river's source grass grew seven or eight feet tall, with red flowers and leaves and seeds green like ox horns.

sentences.zh: 涪陵民藥氏婦頭上生角，長三寸，凡三截之。

translations.literal: A woman of the Yao clan in Fuling grew a horn on her head, three inches long; it was cut off three times in all.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Yao clan in Fuling grew a horn on her head three inches long. It was cut off three times in all.

sentences.zh: 李漢家舂米，米自臼中跳出，斂舉箕中，又跳出，寫置簟中。

translations.literal: In Li Han's household they pounded rice; the rice leaped from the mortar, was gathered into a winnowing basket, leaped out again, and was swept onto a mat.
translations.idiomatic: In Li Han's household they pounded rice. The rice leaped from the mortar into the winnowing basket, leaped out again, and was swept onto a mat.

sentences.zh: 童謠曰：「江橋頭，闕下市，成都北門十八子。」

translations.literal: A children's rhyme said: 'At the head of the river bridge, below the tower market, at Chengdu's north gate—eighteen sons.'
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme said, "At the head of the river bridge, below the tower market, at Chengdu's north gate—eighteen sons."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「有客有客，來侵門陌，其氣欲索。」

translations.literal: Again it said: 'There is a guest, there is a guest, coming to invade the gate and lane; his qi seeks to seize.'
translations.idiomatic: Another rhyme said, "There is a guest, there is a guest, coming to invade the gate and lane; his breath seeks to seize."

sentences.zh: 譙周云：「我死後三十年，當有異人入蜀，由之而亡。」

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou said: 'Thirty years after I die, there will be an extraordinary man entering Shu; through him it will perish.'
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou said, "Thirty years after I die, an extraordinary man will enter Shu, and through him the state will perish."

sentences.zh: 蜀亡之歲，去周亡三十二年。

translations.literal: The year Shu perished was thirty-two years from Zhou's death.
translations.idiomatic: The year Shu perished was thirty-two years after Zhou's death.

sentences.zh: 周又著讖曰：「廣漢城北，有大賊，曰流特，攻難得，歲在玄宮自相克。」

translations.literal: Zhou also composed a prophecy: 'North of Guanghan city, there is a great bandit called Liu Te; hard to attack and take; in the year of the Dark Palace they will destroy each other.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhou also composed a prophecy: "North of Guanghan city there is a great bandit called Liu Te, hard to attack and overcome. In the year of the Dark Palace they will destroy each other."

sentences.zh: 卒如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it came to pass as he had said.

translations.literal: Commentary
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：司馬叡之竄江表，竊魁帥之名，無君長之實，跼天蹐地，畏首畏尾，對之李雄，各一方小盜，其孫皓之不若矣。

translations.literal: The history ministers say: Sima Rui's flight to the lands south of the Yangtze stole the name of a chief commander without the substance of a lord; cramped between Heaven and Earth, fearful of head and tail—compared with Li Xiong, each a petty robber in one corner, he was not the equal of his grandson Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The historians say: Sima Rui's flight south of the Yangtze stole the title of a chief commander without the substance of a true ruler. Cramped and fearful, he was but a petty robber in one corner—compared with Li Xiong, and not even the equal of his grandson Sun Hao.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 迎其母俱歸陳國 按晉書卷五元帝紀云：「迎太妃俱歸國。」

translations.literal: 'Welcoming his mother to return together to the State of Chen'—according to the Basic Annals of Emperor Yuan in Jin Shu, volume 5: 'Welcoming the Grand Consort to return together to the state.'
translations.idiomatic: "Welcoming his mother to return together to the State of Chen": According to the Basic Annals of Emperor Yuan in Jin Shu, volume 5: "Welcoming the Grand Consort to return together to the state."

sentences.zh: 「歸國」指歸司馬叡受封的瑯邪國。

translations.literal: Return to the state' refers to returning to the state of Langye, where Sima Rui had been enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Return to the state" refers to returning to the state of Langye, where Sima Rui had been enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 這時陳郡沒有王，不是國，且和司馬叡無關，不得云「歸」。

translations.literal: At this time Chen Commandery had no king, was not a state, and had no relation to Sima Rui; one cannot say 'return.'
translations.idiomatic: At this time Chen Commandery had no prince, was not a feudal state, and had no connection to Sima Rui. One cannot say "return."

sentences.zh: 「陳」字當衍，或字訛。

translations.literal: The character 'Chen' is probably superfluous, or the character is corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: The character "Chen" is probably superfluous, or the character is corrupt.

sentences.zh: 當鎮壽陽 按壽陽即壽春，東晉司馬昱

translations.literal: 'Was to garrison Shouyang'—note Shouyang is Shouchun; Eastern Jin's Sima Yu
translations.idiomatic: "Was to garrison Shouyang": Note that Shouyang is Shouchun. Eastern Jin's Sima Yu

sentences.zh: 〈簡文帝〉

translations.literal: 〈Emperor Jianwen〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emperor Jianwen〉

sentences.zh: 母鄭太后名「阿春」，始改「壽陽」

translations.literal: mother Empress Dowager Zheng named 'Achun' first changed 'Shouyang'
translations.idiomatic: whose mother Empress Dowager Zheng was named "Achun" first changed the name to "Shouyang"

sentences.zh: 〈見太平寰宇記卷一二九壽州條〉，

translations.literal: 〈see Taiping Imperial Reader, juan 129, Shouzhou entry〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈see Taiping Imperial Reader, juan 129, Shouzhou entry〉

sentences.zh: 這時應作「壽春」。

translations.literal: at this time it should read 'Shouchun.'
translations.idiomatic: At this time it should read "Shouchun."

sentences.zh: 平東府事 按此四字不可解，「東府」或指東中郎府，然不見晉書卷六元帝紀，疑有誤。

translations.literal: 'Affairs of the Pacify-the-East headquarters'—note these four characters are inexplicable; 'Eastern headquarters' may refer to the Eastern Central Commander headquarters, yet it is not seen in Jin Shu, juan 6, Basic Annals of Emperor Yuan; there is probably an error.
translations.idiomatic: "Affairs of the Pacify-the-East headquarters": These four characters are inexplicable. "Eastern headquarters" may refer to the Eastern Central Commander headquarters, yet it does not appear in Jin Shu, juan 6, Basic Annals of Emperor Yuan. There is probably an error.

sentences.zh: 今趣進軍 晉書卷九八王敦傳「趣」作「輒」。

translations.literal: 'Now urge the army forward'—in Jin Shu, juan 98, Biography of Wang Dun, 'urge' is written as 'at once.'
translations.idiomatic: "Now urge the army forward": In Jin Shu, juan 98, Biography of Wang Dun, "urge" is written as "at once."

sentences.zh: 按文義當作「輒」，「趣」乃形近而訛。

translations.literal: According to the sense of the text it should be 'at once'; 'urge' is a corruption through similar form.
translations.idiomatic: According to the sense of the text it should read "at once"; "urge" is a corruption through similar form.

sentences.zh: 紹平西將軍祖約率眾至于淮南 諸本脫「將」字，據晉書卷六明帝紀太寧二年五月及七月條、卷一００祖約傳補。

translations.literal: 'Shao's General Who Pacifies the West Zu Yue led masses to Huainan'—various editions omit the character 'general'; supplemented according to Jin Shu, juan 6, Basic Annals of Emperor Ming, fifth and seventh month entries of the second year of Taining, and juan 100, Biography of Zu Yue.
translations.idiomatic: "Shao's General Who Pacifies the West Zu Yue led masses to Huainan": Various editions omit the character "general," supplemented according to Jin Shu, juan 6, Basic Annals of Emperor Ming, fifth and seventh month entries of the second year of Taining, and juan 100, Biography of Zu Yue.

sentences.zh: 自以四馬北下突陳 晉書卷一００蘇峻傳「四馬」作「數騎」。

translations.literal: 'Himself with four horses charged north down into the formation'—in Jin Shu, juan 100, Biography of Su Jun, 'four horses' is written as 'several horsemen.'
translations.idiomatic: "Himself with four horses charged north into the formation": In Jin Shu, juan 100, Biography of Su Jun, "four horses" is written as "several horsemen."

sentences.zh: 疑「四馬」當是「匹馬」或「四騎」之訛。

translations.literal: It is suspected 'four horses' should be 'one horse' or 'four riders'—a corruption.
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected that "four horses" should be "one horse" or "four riders"—a corruption.

sentences.zh: 乃發衍父母冢 晉書卷一００蘇峻傳作「發庾亮父母墓」。

translations.literal: 'Then opened Yan's parents' tomb'—in Jin Shu, juan 100, Biography of Su Jun, it reads 'opened Yu Liang's parents' tomb.'
translations.idiomatic: "Then opened Yan's parents' tomb": In Jin Shu, juan 100, Biography of Su Jun, it reads "opened Yu Liang's parents' tomb."

sentences.zh: 按衍父即晉明帝司馬紹，不聞其墓被發，「衍」疑當作「亮」。

translations.literal: Note Yan's father is Emperor Ming of Jin Sima Shao; it is not heard that his tomb was opened; 'Yan' is suspected to be 'Liang.'
translations.idiomatic: Note that Yan's father was Emperor Ming of Jin, Sima Shao. There is no record of his tomb being opened. "Yan" is suspected to be "Liang."

sentences.zh: 德宗遣廣武將軍玄文石齊朝貢 按「玄文石齊」疑有誤，卷三太宗紀不記晉使姓名，無可參證。

translations.literal: 'Dezong sent General of Broad Martial Might Xuan Wen Shi Qi with tribute'—note 'Xuan Wen Shi Qi' is suspected to be in error; juan 3, Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong, does not record the Jin envoy's name, and there is nothing for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: "Dezong sent General of Broad Martial Might Xuan Wen Shi Qi with tribute": "Xuan Wen Shi Qi" is suspected to be in error. Juan 3, Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong, does not record the Jin envoy's name, and there is nothing for comparison.

sentences.zh: 今姑作二人標。

translations.literal: For now they are tentatively marked as two persons.
translations.idiomatic: For now they are tentatively marked as two persons.

sentences.zh: 二年太宗遣長孫道生娥清破其將朱超石於石河 諸本「二年」作「三年」。

translations.literal: 'In the second year Emperor Taizong sent Zhangsun Daosheng and E Qing to defeat his general Zhu Chaoshi at Shihe'—various editions read 'third year' for 'second year.'
translations.idiomatic: "In the second year Emperor Taizong sent Zhangsun Daosheng and E Qing to defeat his general Zhu Chaoshi at Shihe": Various editions read "third year" for "second year."

sentences.zh: 按卷三太宗紀泰常二年二月記：「詔司徒長孫嵩率諸軍邀擊劉裕，戰於畔城。」

translations.literal: According to juan 3, Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong, second month of the second year of Taichang: 'An edict ordered Minister of Education Zhangsun Song to lead the armies to intercept and strike Liu Yu; they fought at Pancheng.'
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 3, Basic Annals of Emperor Taizong, second month of the second year of Taichang: "An edict ordered Minister of Education Zhangsun Song to lead the armies to intercept Liu Yu. They fought at Pancheng."

sentences.zh: 據卷九七劉裕傳云：「始裕入河西 上，太宗遣將軍娥清、長孫嵩等屯於河畔。

translations.literal: According to juan 97, Biography of Liu Yu: 'When Yu first entered Hexi, Emperor Taizong sent Generals E Qing, Zhangsun Song, and others to encamp on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 97, Biography of Liu Yu: "When Yu first entered Hexi, Emperor Taizong sent Generals E Qing, Zhangsun Song, and others to encamp on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 裕遣朱超石、劉榮祖等渡河，長孫道生破之，擒斬其 將楊豐等。」

translations.literal: Yu sent Zhu Chaoshi, Liu Rongzu, and others across the river; Zhangsun Daosheng defeated them, captured and beheaded his general Yang Feng and others.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Zhu Chaoshi, Liu Rongzu, and others across the river. Zhangsun Daosheng defeated them and captured and beheaded his general Yang Feng and others."

sentences.zh: 卷三０娥青傳記此事作「朱超石寇平原，至畔城遁還」。

translations.literal: Juan 30, Biography of E Qing, records this affair as 'Zhu Chaoshi raided Pingyuan, reached Pancheng, and fled back.'
translations.idiomatic: Juan 30, Biography of E Qing, records this affair as "Zhu Chaoshi raided Pingyuan, reached Pancheng, and fled back."

sentences.zh: 紀所記即此事，也即此傳 所載破朱超石事。

translations.literal: What the annals record is this affair, and it is also the defeat of Zhu Chaoshi recorded in this biography.
translations.idiomatic: What the annals record is this affair, and it is also the defeat of Zhu Chaoshi recorded in this biography.

sentences.zh: 其事實在泰常二年劉裕北伐時。

translations.literal: The affair in fact occurred when Liu Yu campaigned north in the second year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: The affair in fact occurred during Liu Yu's northern campaign in the second year of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 這裏「三年」乃「二年」之訛，致與下文「三 年，德宗死」重出，今改正。

translations.literal: Here 'third year' is a corruption of 'second year,' causing duplication with the following 'In the third year Dezong died'; it is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Here "third year" is a corruption of "second year," causing duplication with the following "In the third year Dezong died." It is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 口出錢三十 晉書卷一二０李特載記、華陽國志卷九李特志「三十」並作「四十」。

translations.literal: 'Thirty cash per mouth'—in Jin Shu, juan 120, Account of Li Te, and Huayang Guozhi, juan 9, Account of Li Te, both read 'forty' for 'thirty.'
translations.idiomatic: "Thirty cash per mouth": In Jin Shu, juan 120, Account of Li Te, and Huayang Guozhi, juan 9, Account of Li Te, both read "forty" for "thirty."

sentences.zh: 疑這裏「三」 字訛。

translations.literal: It is suspected the character 'three' here is corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected the character "three" here is corrupt.

sentences.zh: 後徙櫟陽 晉書卷一二０李特載記、華陽國志卷九李特志「櫟陽」作「略陽」。

translations.literal: 'Later moved to Liyang'—in Jin Shu, juan 120, Account of Li Te, and Huayang Guozhi, juan 9, Account of Li Te, 'Liyang' is written as 'Lueyang.'
translations.idiomatic: "Later moved to Liyang": In Jin Shu, juan 120, Account of Li Te, and Huayang Guozhi, juan 9, Account of Li Te, "Liyang" is written as "Lueyang."

sentences.zh: 按當時六郡流民 入蜀，略陽是六郡之一。

translations.literal: Note that at the time the refugee masses of the Six Commanderies entered Shu; Lueyang was one of the Six Commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Note that at the time the refugee masses of the Six Commanderies entered Shu. Lueyang was one of the Six Commanderies.

sentences.zh: 櫟陽遠在長安東北

translations.literal: Liyang is far to the northeast of Chang'an
translations.idiomatic: Liyang lies far to the northeast of Chang'an

sentences.zh: 〈今陝西富平〉，

translations.literal: 〈present-day Fuping, Shaanxi〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈present-day Fuping, Shaanxi〉

sentences.zh: 李特若徙居在此，距六郡

translations.literal: if Li Te moved to dwell here, the distance from the Six Commanderies
translations.idiomatic: If Li Te had moved to dwell here, the distance from the Six Commanderies

sentences.zh: 〈今甘肅天水一帶至 陝西鳳翔一帶〉

translations.literal: 〈present-day Tianshui region in Gansu to Fengxiang region in Shaanxi〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈present-day Tianshui region in Gansu to Fengxiang region in Shaanxi〉

sentences.zh: 遙遠，與情勢不合。

translations.literal: would be remote, not matching the situation.
translations.idiomatic: would be too remote and does not match the situation.

sentences.zh: 「櫟陽」乃「略陽」之訛。

translations.literal: 'Liyang' is a corruption of 'Lueyang.'
translations.idiomatic: "Liyang" is a corruption of "Lueyang."

sentences.zh: 發州郡工巧以充之 諸本「郡」訛「都」，今據晉書卷一二一李壽載記改。

translations.literal: 'Mobilized skilled artisans from provinces and commanderies to fill them'—various editions corrupt 'commandery' as 'capital'; now corrected according to Jin Shu, juan 121, Account of Li Shou.
translations.idiomatic: "Mobilized skilled artisans from provinces and commanderies to fill them": Various editions corrupt "commandery" as "capital." Now corrected according to Jin Shu, juan 121, Account of Li Shou.
